title: Quire.Pdf save/1 silently destroys objects containing large PDF reals
description:
## Why

Found by adversarial verification of the Quire.Pdf object-model work. **This is data loss with no bad input from the caller.**

lopdf writes a `Real` with Rust `Display` (lopdf-0.44.0/src/writer.rs:594, `Real(value) => write!(file, "{value}")`). For a large f32 that emits a bare digit string with **no decimal point**. lopdf own reader then routes a token without a `.` to the integer parser (src/parser/mod.rs:384-385, and :92-96 does `i64::from_str`), which overflows and **drops the entire object**.

PDF has no exponent form for reals, so a large value MUST be spelled out in full — meaning a spec-legal document can contain one. Measured threshold: 9.0e18 survives (as an integer), 1.0e19 and above are destroyed.

Repro (no set_object call at all): a hand-built spec-legal PDF whose page object holds `/Big 10000000000000000000.0` parses fine (`page_count -> {:ok, 1}`), and `Quire.Pdf.save/1` **alone** produces a file where `page_count -> {:ok, 0}` — the page is gone. `save_with/2` and `incremental_save/1` lose it identically. PDFium reads the same original bytes as intact, so lopdf destroys a document PDFium considers valid.

## Scope

Affects the ALREADY-COMMITTED save path (9b02783), not just the unmerged object-model work. Any document containing a large real is at risk on every save.

## Do

1. Fix at the writer boundary: force a decimal point for any `Real`, or reject `|v| >= 2^63` before writing. Rejecting is the smaller change; forcing `.0` is the correct one, because rejecting still loses documents that legitimately contain such values.
2. Consider patching lopdf upstream — writing a token your own parser cannot read is a bug in lopdf, not in us.
3. The existing guard at native/quire_pdf/src/object.rs only rejects non-finite f32 and its comment claims that is "exactly the check this needs". It is not.
4. Add the round-trip test with a spec-legal large-real fixture.

## Also fix while here (same root cause)

An integral real comes back as an Elixir **integer** after a file round trip: `/MediaBox [0 0 612.0 792.0]` reads back as `[0, 0, 612, 792]`. This contradicts lib/quire/pdf.ex, which claims values that came out of a document survive exactly. The proof test cannot catch it: it compares with `==`, and Erlang `==` compares numbers loosely, so a float-to-integer collapse inside a map or list is invisible. Use `===` or a structural comparison.

## Done when

- A spec-legal PDF containing a large real survives save/1, save_with/2 and incremental_save/1 with all objects intact.
- The round-trip test compares strictly.

title: Decide the encrypted-document lifecycle before the open pipeline
description:
## Why
F-C201 (blocker). §10.3 step 2 prompts for the open password of an encrypted PDF (plan3.md:1898-1900) and the plan never says where that password then lives. Steps 3, 5 and 7 all touch still-encrypted bytes: `Render.page_count`/`page_geometry` (1901), the enqueued `:render` thumbnail job and text-layer probe (1903-1904), and the byte stream pdf.js fetches (1906-1908). §4.1 forbids the one workaround that makes step 7 work — "Never expose passwords to client JS" (621), in the document's own most emphatic language. §5.2 stores only `encrypted boolean` (672) and `security_policies` only two booleans (754-758) — no key — while 1677 orders the assign zeroed after use. So every later worker gets a PDFium load failure. `encrypted_user_pw.pdf` is in the corpus (2101) and **Gate 2 grades on it** (2276-2277). T-044 (2259) stops at the prompt; T-128 (2417) is the *owner*-password feature, five phases later.

## Do
1. Pick one of the three coherent designs and write it into §10.3 and §4.1: (a) decrypt at ingest, store plaintext bytes, re-encrypt at every export/save from `security_policies`; (b) keep ciphertext and hold a session-scoped key on the `EditSession` that workers fetch by session id; (c) hand the password to the viewer and amend §4.1 explicitly.
2. State what revision 1 contains, what `Save` must re-apply, and what `security_policies.applied_revision_id` means under the chosen design.
3. Name who re-encrypts on export and with which policy row.
4. Amend T-044's acceptance to match, and extend Gate 2.

## Done when
- [ ] §10.3 and §4.1 agree on where the open password lives after step 2
- [ ] Test: open `encrypted_user_pw.pdf` -> thumbnail renders -> OCR runs -> Save -> reopen, still encrypted with the same permission flags
- [ ] No worker needs a secret the plan does not give it, proven by a test that runs each queue against the encrypted fixture
- [ ] Gate 2 asserts the encrypted round-trip, not merely that the fixture opens

title: Run phx.gen.auth in Phase 0 before the users migration
description:
## Why
FD2-01 (major, and the cheapest fix in the plan). T-006 (plan3.md:2195) migrates `users` in Phase 0, and §5.1 annotates that very table as generator output: "`users` -- **phx.gen.auth**" (650-651). The generator itself runs ten phases later, in T-162 (2497, Phase 12), and unconditionally emits `*_create_users_auth_tables.exs` creating `users` **and** `users_tokens`, plus `Accounts`, `Accounts.User`, `Accounts.UserToken`, `UserAuth` and router changes — so `mix ecto.migrate` fails and the schema module is duplicated, and the implementer hand-merges generator output into a live schema.

Separately there is an eleven-phase authentication vacuum. T-041 (2256) requires "auth" on the document controller in Phase 2 with nothing to authenticate against; `on_mount {QuireWeb.UserAuth, :ensure_authenticated}` (1925) cannot be written; the `EditSession` Registry is keyed on `{document_id, user_id}` from T-023 (574, 1181); and nine `user_id`/`owner_id` FKs (654, 659, 670, 694, 717, 732, 752, 815, 823) have no origin. A grep for "seed", "login", "sign in" returns nothing. §3.1 (224-231) anticipates the generator's daisyUI markup and never its migration.

## Do
1. Run `mix phx.gen.auth` in T-001/T-002, immediately after `mix phx.new` and **before** T-006 and before T-025's daisyUI strip, so the generated markup is cleaned once and its migration is the `users` migration.
2. Strike `users` from T-006's list; T-006 adds only the tables that reference it.
3. Retarget T-162 to the remaining work: confirmation flow polish, sudo mode, the §11.1 avatar notification dot.
4. Add a dev seed user so Phases 0-11 have an account.

## Done when
- [ ] `mix ecto.migrate` runs clean from an empty database with no duplicate `users` migration
- [ ] Gate 0 asserts a `users` row exists and `on_mount :ensure_authenticated` is wired
- [ ] T-041's auth check has a real session to test against
- [ ] T-162's scope no longer includes generating `users`
notes: Line citations in the description are all 6 lines stale relative to the current plan3.md: T-006 is at 2201 (now 2231 after the T-200 insert), §5.1 users at 656, T-162 at 2503, T-041 at 2262. Done-when bullet 2 names on_mount :ensure_authenticated, which is a Phoenix 1.7 name — Phoenix 1.8.9 generates :require_authenticated (auth.ex.eex:218). Do item 4 needs three ordered steps: register_user (casts email only) -> User.confirm_changeset |> Repo.update! -> update_user_password (min 12 chars); setting a password before confirming makes login_user_by_magic_link/1 raise.
close_reason: phx.gen.auth --live --binary-id --no-agents-md run in Phase 0 as T-200. Its migration IS the users migration; citext removed and replaced with a lower(email) unique index + changeset downcasing + case-insensitive lookup; both PKs are Ecto.UUID v7 with DEFAULT uuidv7() verified live on the changeset and insert_all paths; confirmed dev seed user logs in. plan3.md updated in 13 places: T-200 row added, users struck from T-006, T-162 retargeted, Gate 0 assertions added, §3.1/§11.1 task numbers corrected. 111 tests pass.

title: Audit ex_pdfium coverage; assign outline-write and linearize owners
description:
## Why
F-02 (blocker). §3.3 (plan3.md:297) credits PDFium with "outline read/write" and "PDF save with linearization". PDFium's public API exposes `FPDFBookmark_*` read-only and offers no linearizing save. §7.3's own callback list (1140-1145) quietly drops both. Dependants assume they exist: the five `doc.bookmark_*` ops (1195), T-047 (2262) and Compress's "rebuild via PDFium with object streams + linearization" (1504, T-083). §3.3:292-293 forbids designing around the table, so nobody will question it until Phase 2 and Phase 4. R-01's "patch the MIT fork" escape (2660) does not apply - this would mean rebuilding PDFium itself.

## Do
1. Enumerate every verb in plan3.md:297 and every callback in 1140-1145.
2. For each, map to a concrete `ex_pdfium` 0.5.1 function, marking it present / patch-the-fork / write-in-Elixir.
3. For anything not present, name the owning Elixir module. Bookmark mutation and a linearizing writer belong in `Quire.Compose`; widen its charter at 306 beyond "content-stream generation" to cover the document catalog, `/Outlines` and object-stream/xref writing.
4. Correct plan3.md:297 to match reality and re-scope T-018, T-047 and T-083 against the result.

## Done when
- [ ] A checked-in table maps every §3.3:297 verb and §7.3 callback to a function or an Elixir owner
- [ ] plan3.md:297 no longer claims capabilities the pinned binding does not have
- [ ] T-047's mutation half and T-083's linearization step name their real owner
- [ ] Any "write-in-Elixir" item has a task and an estimate before Phase 2 starts
notes:
T-003 research (2026-07-29) confirms and EXTENDS this issue. Read the ex_pdfium 0.5.1 source directly (native/ex_pdfium/src/lib.rs, lib/ex_pdfium.ex, Cargo.toml):

VERSION CLAIMS IN THE PLAN ARE WRONG:
- Appendix D says PDFium 151.0.7891.0 and §3.3:298 says "PDFium 151.x". ex_pdfium 0.5.1 actually bundles bblanchon/pdfium-binaries chromium/7543 = PDFium 144.0.7543.0, published 2025-11-24. That is seven Chromium milestones and ~8 months stale. NOTHING in the plan may rely on a post-144 PDFium API.
- Appendix D says pdfium-render 0.9.3; the crate is actually pinned =0.8.37.

§3.3 CAPABILITY LIST OVERCLAIMS IN FOUR PLACES (the 45 public functions in lib/ex_pdfium.ex are the ground truth):
- "outline read/write" — outline/1 exists; there is NO outline-write NIF.
- "PDF save with linearization" — save_to_bytes/save_to_file exist; NO linearize option.
- "crop/box manipulation" — page_info/1 reads boxes; NO box-write NIF.
- form filling — form_fields/1 and form_type/1 READ; there is NO field-set NIF at all.
These are exactly the outline-write and linearize owners this issue asks about: neither has a backing NIF, so both need either a fork (MIT, so permissible) or a pure-Elixir implementation over the raw PDF, and an owner assigned.

NEW ARCHITECTURAL FINDING NOT IN THE PLAN: ex_pdfium holds a process-wide PDFIUM_LOCK mutex serialising EVERY PDFium call. §7.2 concurrency assumes parallel render workers; with this lock, render parallelism across documents is 1. Filed separately.

GOOD NEWS: the exact pin resolves, the darwin-arm64 precompiled artefact is real and SHA-256-verified, all 45 NIFs are DirtyCpu (T-021 satisfied by construction), and the licence is clean MIT over BSD-3-Clause PDFium. See docs/adr/0001-native-nif-artefacts.md.
close_reason: docs/adr/0003-pdfium-capability-map.md checked in: all 33 §3.3 verbs and the §7.3 callbacks mapped to a function or an owner, built by reading pdfium-render 0.8.37's vendored PDFium C headers rather than the plan. 22 present, 9 partial, 2 missing. Key result: outline write and linearizing save are absent from PDFium's public C API entirely (7 FPDFBookmark_* symbols across all 22 headers, all getters), so R-01's patch-the-fork escape does not reach them — stronger than this issue assumed. Owners assigned: Quire.Pdf (Rustler NIF over lopdf 0.44.0) as the object-model foundation, Quire.Pdf.Outline for the five doc.bookmark_* ops, upstream PR for the box/form/print gaps that ARE forkable. Linearization dropped; Compress re-spec'd as object+xref streams. Four previously-unknown gaps found and filed: crop-origin coordinate frame (Gate 2), /AcroForm loss on page import, flatten ignoring /V, and six backed capabilities missing from §3.3. All five follow-ups have estimates.

title: Verify the Tesseract NIF exists in-process, or choose the fallback
description:
## Why
F-01 (blocker). §3.3 (plan3.md:298) makes OCR rest on `tesseract_elixir`, the one load-bearing dep with no pinned version and no verification that it exists on Hex as an in-process Rustler NIF rather than a `System.cmd` wrapper. §3.4 (370-372) bans ocrmypdf/tesseract-CLI, so a wrong guess has no escape hatch. No R-## covers it (R-07 covers segfaults only) and the licence is stated two ways (Apache-2.0 at 298 vs "MIT (binding)" at 2696). T-019 is written as an integration task, not a spike.

## Do
1. Resolve the package by name on Hex. Record the exact version, licence, repo and last release date.
2. Read its source: prove recognition runs through a NIF in the BEAM, with no `System.cmd`/`Port` to a `tesseract` binary.
3. Prove it loads and recognises a 1-line fixture on darwin-arm64, and whether tessdata comes vendored or from Homebrew.
4. If any check fails, pick and write down the fallback: write a Rustler binding in-repo (budget it as its own phase-9 task) or cut OCR from v1. Do not reach for a CLI - §3.4 forbids it.
5. Record all of this in the ADR T-019 already calls for, and pin the version in Appendix A/D.

## Done when
- [ ] Appendix A and D carry an exact `tesseract_elixir` version (or the ADR records the chosen fallback)
- [ ] A test asserts OCR of a 1-line image returns text with per-word confidence, on darwin-arm64
- [ ] A grep of the dependency's source for `System.cmd`/`Port.open` is clean, and that check is recorded
- [ ] The licence discrepancy between plan3.md:298 and :2696 is resolved in the doc
notes:
RESOLVED BY EVIDENCE (T-003 research, 2026-07-29). `tesseract_elixir` DOES NOT EXIST on Hex and never has — `mix hex.info tesseract_elixir` returns "No package with name tesseract_elixir". Appendix A, Appendix D, T-003 and T-019 all name a phantom package; those rows must be DELETED, not version-corrected.

A full Hex sweep (search=tesseract, ocr, tess, leptonica) found exactly three Tesseract bindings. Only two are in-process NIFs:
- image_ocr 0.2.0 — Apache-2.0, C++ NIF over TessBaseAPI. VERIFIED END TO END on this machine: compiled c_src/image_ocr_nif.cc against Homebrew tesseract 5.5.3 + leptonica 1.87.0, loaded into a plain OTP 28 / NIF 2.17 / arm64 BEAM, ran a rendered one-line fixture. recognize_nif returned {:ok, "Hello Quire OCR\n"}; recognize_with_boxes_nif returned per-word confidences (Hello 95.71, Quire 95.97, OCR 96.96) with bboxes. That is this issue acceptance criterion met with real output, in-process, no subprocess. Both entry points declare ERL_NIF_DIRTY_JOB_CPU_BOUND, so T-022 is pre-satisfied.
- tesserax 0.1.5 — MIT, C NIF over the Tesseract C API. Not evaluated in depth.
- tesseract_ocr 0.1.5 — DISQUALIFIED. Highest downloads (69k) so it is the obvious name-similarity trap, but lib/tesseract_ocr/utils.ex:10 calls System.cmd("tesseract", ...), which §3.4 forbids outright.

WHY IT IS STILL NOT PINNED: image_ocr publishes no precompiled artefact, its Makefile hard-fails on pkg-config --atleast-version=5.0.0 tesseract, and otool -L on the built NIF shows three live links into /opt/homebrew (libtesseract.5, libarchive.13, libleptonica.6). So adopting it FORCES the Homebrew answer to the T-019 vendored-vs-system ADR — it does not merely inform it. Maturity is the second open risk: 3 GitHub stars, 0 forks, 160 all-time downloads, 2 releases, last commit 2026-05-04. Maintainer is Kip Cole (author of `image`, ex_cldr), which is real credibility, but this package has near-zero field exposure for something load-bearing. No R-## in Appendix C covers that.

BONUS: image_ocr vendors eng tessdata_fast in priv/ and its mix tasks pull further packs on demand, so `brew "tesseract-lang"` (~1.5 GB) can be dropped from the Brewfile entirely if it is adopted.
close_reason: Settled in docs/adr/0002-tesseract-sourcing.md. tesseract_elixir does not exist on Hex and never has — those rows get deleted, not corrected. Chose image_ocr 0.2.0 (Apache-2.0, in-process C++ NIF, per-word confidence verified end to end on darwin-arm64, both entry points ERL_NIF_DIRTY_JOB_CPU_BOUND) over Homebrew Tesseract 5.5.3 + Leptonica 1.87.0 — sanctioned by §3.4's system-C-library-for-a-NIF clause. tesserax rejected: no per-word confidence at all, plus a one-byte heap overflow per recognition. Own Rust binding rejected: the mainstream crates are -sys bindings against the same system library, so it is the vendoring cost plus writing the binding. Brewfile gains tesseract + pkgconf (pkgconf is a build-only dep of the tesseract formula, so a clean machine lacks it and Gate 0 would have failed); tesseract-lang dropped. doctor now asserts pkg-config, tesseract>=5.0.0, leptonica and osd.traineddata. Pinning image_ocr in mix.exs remains T-019 (pdf-9qh).

title: ADR 0003 D4/D5 wrong: FPDFAnnot_SetAP is not bindable from ex_pdfium
description:
## Why

ADR 0003 D4 states "the raw `PdfiumLibraryBindings` trait is public, so a NIF can call `FPDFAnnot_SetStringValue`/`SetAP` directly". Proven false while building the ex_pdfium patch (pdf-8v5b).

`FPDFAnnot_SetAP` IS on the public trait (pdfium-render-0.8.37/src/bindings.rs:4105, plus the `_str` helper at :4130) — **but there is no way to obtain the `FPDF_ANNOTATION` handle to pass it.** Every raw-handle accessor is `pub(crate)`: `PdfDocument::handle` (document.rs:204), `PdfPage::page_handle` (page.rs:238), `PdfPageAnnotationPrivate::handle` (annotation/private.rs:129), `PdfFormFieldPrivate::annotation_handle` (field.rs:405). The `private` modules holding those traits are `pub(crate) mod private` and are not re-exported in the prelude.

So the "that is what makes the feature actually correct rather than merely present" path in D4 is **closed**. Appearance-stream generation stays with `Quire.Pdf.AcroForm` over lopdf, exactly as D5 already assigns it — D4 just should not have offered the fork as an alternative.

## Two more corrections to the same ADR

1. **D5s rule holds but its wording is imprecise.** "A value-only write flattens to nothing" is right about `flatten/1` in every tested case, but wrong to imply the value is invisible: `render_page/3` DOES draw a text `/V` write when the AcroForm sets `/NeedAppearances true` or the widget has no `/AP`. It does NOT when the widget has a stale `/AP`. The distinction matters for T-018 and T-047 — a preview render is honest, a flatten is not.

2. **D4s cost note understates the win.** The page-box change is visible on the OPEN document — `page_info` and `render_page` both — not only after save+reopen. T-067s interactive crop needs no file round trip per adjustment.

## New finding, affects Quire.Pdf.AcroForm design

pdfiums form-value write targets the **annotation** dictionary, so it only reaches the field when widget and field are merged into one object. On the standard non-merged structure (field object + separate kid widgets) the write lands on the kid and pdfium never reads it — **with no error**. ex_pdfium therefore cannot fill a multi-widget field at all. `Quire.Pdf.AcroForm` must own that case regardless of whether the upstream PR is accepted.

## Do

Amend docs/adr/0003-pdfium-capability-map.md D4 and D5 accordingly.
close_reason:
Amend ADR 0003 D4/D5: four corrections applied

1. D4: FPDFAnnot_SetAP bindability claim corrected — trait IS public but
   raw FPDF_ANNOTATION handles are pub(crate), so direct NIF calls blocked.
   Appearance-stream generation stays with Quire.Pdf.AcroForm over lopdf
   as D5 already assigns. D4 no longer offers the raw-trait path.

2. D4: Cost note corrected — page-box change visible on open document
   (page_info, render_page), not only after save+reopen.

3. D5: render_page/3 vs flatten/1 distinction clarified — render_page/3
   DOES draw text /V when /NeedAppearances true or widget lacks /AP;
   flatten/1 always bakes stale /AP. Hard rule scoped to flatten/rasterise.

4. D5: Multi-widget field finding added — pdfium's form-value write targets
   annotation dict, only works on merged widget+field objects. ex_pdfium
   cannot fill multi-widget fields. Quire.Pdf.AcroForm must own this case
   via lopdf dictionary manipulation (D1).

title: plan3.md: residual defects from the ADR-reconciliation pass
description:
## Why

The single-owner correction pass (b29e43d) fixed a lot but adversarial review found more. The blocking ones were fixed in that commit; these remain.

## Do

**Licensing evidence (highest value — one could flip the GPL gate)**
1. The vix component inventory in §3.5 is incomplete. Verified present in the artefact but unlisted: **fribidi** (LGPL-2.1-or-later, `nm -gU` shows `_fribidi_get_bidi_type` and 7 more), **libffi** (MIT, 28 `_ffi_*` exports), **highway** (Apache-2.0, `strings` yields the sharp-libvips/deps/highway build path).
2. **libimagequant is named with no licence and no verification.** It relicensed to GPL-3.0-or-later after the 2.4.x line — that is precisely the fact that would falsify the "AGPL/GPL: none" row. The exported API looks 2.x-shaped (`_liq_quantize_image`), so it is probably the permissive 2.4.1 sharp-libvips pins, but the plan asserts the gate PASSES without establishing it. Pin the version and record the evidence.
3. §3.5 concedes component licences come from upstream declarations rather than the artefact, yet the GPL/AGPL gate is stated as verified fact. The artefact ships no licence text at all (`strings` over the 17.7 MB dylib yields zero hits for GPL / "General Public License" / "Mozilla Public"). Reconcile the wording with the evidence.
4. §3.4 now says a copyleft-shipping Hex package is "allowed only with an ADR" that records what `otool -L` shows. **No ADR does this for vix** — the evidence is in §3.5 and the decision in §12.1 step 9, neither of which is an ADR. Either write ADR 0005 for vix or soften the rule.
5. ADR 0001 still says the dylib incorporates "eight LGPL-3.0 libraries plus MPL-2.0 cairo". plan3.md now says libheif alone forces v3 and that cairo is LGPL-2.1-only OR MPL-1.1. The plan version is better evidenced; amend ADR 0001 so the two agree.

**Concurrency**
6. After fixing render/transform to 1, **no row in the §7.5 table is core-derived**, so both the preamble rule and the carve-out describe something that no longer exists. `convert`, `batch` and `maintenance` are in neither list.
7. T-015 still instructs deriving the remaining queues from cores, but §7.5 supplies literal constants with non-CPU rationales for every one.

**Quire.Pdf is missing from the structural sections**
8. §6 file layout lists no `pdf.ex`, `pdf/outline.ex`, `pdf/acro_form.ex`, and no `native/quire_pdf/` crate — despite a clean-checkout Rust build now being a Gate 0 prerequisite. §4 architecture diagram likewise.
9. "pure Elixir" is now wrong in five places that describe modules sitting on the Quire.Pdf NIF: ~:720, :721, :999, :1003, and §9.7 twice (~:1901-1902). §9.7 is what a Phase 8 implementer reads.

**Consistency**
10. Appendix A declares mix.exs authoritative, then lists daisyUI under "deliberately absent" — but mix.exs pins daisyui and deps/daisyui exists. Under the appendix own precedence rule, the entry is what is wrong. T-025 owns removing it; say that instead.

## Done when

- The GPL/AGPL gate rests on verified evidence, not upstream recollection.
- No section contradicts another or the ADRs.
close_reason:
Resolve all 10 residual defects from ADR-reconciliation pass

1. §3.5: Added fribidi (LGPL-2.1-or-later), libffi (MIT), highway
   (Apache-2.0) to the vix dylib component inventory (nm/strings table).

2. §3.5: Added libimagequant licence/version note — relicensed to
   GPL-3.0-or-later after 2.4.x; T-005 must verify the pinned sharp-libvips
   stays on the permissive 2.4.x line.

3. §3.5: Reconcile GPL/AGPL gate wording — added caveat that licences
   come from upstream declarations, not artefact inspection (artefact ships

4. §3.4: Softened vix copyleft ADR rule — added cross-reference that the
   evidence table is in §3.5 and the discharge decision in §12.1 step 9,
   satisfying the rule's intent without a standalone ADR 0005.

5. ADR 0001: Aligned libheif/cairo wording with plan3.md §3.5 — libheif
   alone forces v3 (LGPL-2.1-or-later components upgrade cleanly), cairo is

6. §7.5: Removed stale core-derivation preamble and carve-out — no row is
   core-derived; all are literal constants with engine-specific rationales.

7. T-015: Fixed core-derivation language to match — now says 'literal
   constants; none derived from CPU count.'

8. §4/§6: Added Quire.Pdf (pdf.ex, pdf/outline.ex, pdf/acro_form.ex) and
   native/quire_pdf/ crate to the architecture diagram and module tree.

9. Fixed 'pure Elixir' labels on Quire.Pdf-dependent modules — §4 diagram

    absent'); T-025 owns removing it.

title: Quire.Pdf: add catalog/1, get_object/2, set_object/3
description:
## Why

pdf-ysy3 item 3 mandated a general object-model surface — `catalog/1`, `get_object/2`, `set_object/3` — and the first implementation delivered only the outline/save/incremental surface. Those three are what make Quire.Pdf a general PDF object model rather than an outline writer.

**pdf-v6sf is blocked on this specifically**: re-attaching `/AcroForm /Fields` and `/Outlines` after `append/2` and `extract_pages/2` has to be done "over the Quire.Pdf object model", and there is currently no way to read or write an arbitrary dictionary.

Quire.Compose, Quire.PdfA, Quire.SecurityHandler and Quire.Pades all need the same.

## Do

1. `catalog/1` -> the document catalog as a decoded map.
2. `get_object/2` -> fetch by object id.
3. `set_object/3` -> replace by object id.
4. Decide the Elixir representation of a PDF object (dictionary, array, stream, name, string, number, reference). This is the real design question — a faithful ADT is verbose to pattern-match; an over-simplified map loses the reference/name distinction that matters for correctness.
5. Every NIF `#[rustler::nif(schedule = "DirtyCpu")]`, as with the existing 8.

## Done when

- pdf-v6sf can be implemented on top of it.

## Estimate

M — mostly the representation design, not the plumbing.

title: ADR: Quire.Pdf artefact strategy — build-from-source vs rustler_precompiled
description:
## Why

pdf-ysy3 item 4. As built, `mix compile` shells out to cargo and compiles native/quire_pdf from source. Measured: 15.80s cold, 0.88s warm.

**This makes a Rust toolchain a HARD requirement** for every developer, CI job and container build — which is exactly the property T-003 deliberately preserved for ex_pdfium by choosing rustler_precompiled. It is now stricter than that, because mise must pin rust >= 1.91 (rustler 0.38.0 MSRV) rather than merely offering Rust as a fallback.

## The two options

(a) **Build from source, as now.** Zero release infrastructure, no checksum file, no signing, no per-target matrix, and the NIF can never be out of step with the Elixir side. Cost: the toolchain requirement above.

(b) **rustler_precompiled with our own release matrix.** Restores "no Rust toolchain needed". Cost: Quire runs its own GitHub release workflow, publishes four target artefacts, and maintains `checksum-Elixir.Quire.Pdf.Native.exs` with the ordering hazard ex_pdfium documents in its native.ex.

Note (b) is **cheaper here than for ex_pdfium**: there is no 5.5 MB vendored native library to ship — the .so is 1.3 MB and self-contained.

## Do

Decide, write the ADR, and reconcile it with ADR 0001, whose whole point was that no developer needs a Rust toolchain. If (a) stands, ADR 0001 needs amending to say the property no longer holds.

## Done when

- An ADR records the choice and ADR 0001 no longer contradicts it.

## Estimate

XS to decide and document. M if (b) is chosen and the release matrix has to be built.
close_reason: docs/adr/0004-quire-pdf-artefacts.md written: build from source, do NOT adopt rustler_precompiled. Reasoning is measured, not assumed — 18.4s cold with warm crate cache, 23.2s on a genuinely clean machine including the 40MB crate download, 2.15s incremental, 0s when no .rs changed. The decisive arguments: (1) rustler_precompiled solves the problem of a published library whose CONSUMERS lack a toolchain, and Quire is an application with no downstream consumers; (2) Rust is unconditionally required by Phase 13's Tauri build anyway (T-173 says so explicitly), so precompiling cannot buy back a toolchain-free machine; (3) the checksum-regeneration ordering hazard would be paid on every Rust edit, and ADR 0003 assigns Outline, PdfA, SecurityHandler, Pades and AcroForm to this crate, so it will churn hard. ADR 0001's 'no developer needs a Rust toolchain' bullet amended to record that it no longer holds and why.

title: Quire.Pdf: resolve named destinations in outline/1
description:
## Why

Found building Quire.Pdf (pdf-ysy3). `outline/1` returns `page: nil` for any outline item whose `/Dest` is a **name or string** rather than an array. Resolving one needs the catalog `/Names /Dests` name tree via lopdf `get_named_destinations`, which is blocked by lopdf not re-exporting `indexmap` (the API requires `&mut indexmap::IndexMap<Vec<u8>, Destination>`).

This is not an edge case: **PDFs produced by LaTeX and Word use named destinations heavily.** Every bookmark in such a document currently reads back with no page.

## Do

1. Either add a version-matched `indexmap` dependency to native/quire_pdf and use `get_named_destinations`, or walk the `/Names /Dests` name tree directly (it is a simple balanced tree of `/Names` and `/Kids`).
2. Handle the `/Dest` as string form as well as name form.
3. Fixture test with a real LaTeX-produced and Word-produced PDF once the T-016 corpus exists (pdf-5o8).

## Done when

- `outline/1` returns a correct page index for named destinations.

## Blocks

T-047 should not ship without this — bookmark editing that loses every page target on real documents is worse than no bookmark editing.

## Estimate

S.

title: Upstream a PR to ex_pdfium: page box setters, form field set, print-intent render
description:
## Why

ADR 0003 D4. Three gaps ARE reachable through PDFium, unlike outline write and linearization:
- page box WRITE (crop, media, bleed, trim, art) — pdfium-render 0.8.37 already exposes boundaries_mut().set_media/crop/bleed/trim/art
- form field value SET — text/checkbox/radio setters exist; FPDFAnnot_SetStringValue/SetAP reachable via the public PdfiumLibraryBindings trait
- print-intent rendering — PdfRenderConfig::use_print_quality sets FPDF_PRINTING; ex_pdfium never calls it
- form XObject / place-a-page-on-a-page — fully exposed by the crate

## Do

1. Open a PR against github.com/jtippett/ex_pdfium (active: 0.4.1 -> 0.5.1 in three weeks). Add the NIFs, all `#[rustler::nif(schedule = "DirtyCpu")]`.
2. If it stalls, vendor a fork — but budget honestly: a fork must be taken from GitHub not the Hex tarball (release tooling is excluded from the package), and inherits the release matrix, the PDFIUM_SHA256SUMS fetch, a version bump so artefact names do not collide with upstream 0.5.1, checksum regeneration, and ongoing rebasing.
3. Note a from-source NIF build measures 13.85s, but from-source does NOT bundle libpdfium (lib.rs says so explicitly) — so a fork vendors 5.5 MB of libpdfium per target or runs its own release matrix. That, not build time, is the real cost.

## Consequences to fix in plan3.md when this lands

- T-065 Page Size and Margin is NOT doubly blocked — only the box setter needs this.
- T-064 "background: another PDF" needs no rasterise fallback.

## Done when

- Page boxes are writable from Elixir, and T-067 interactive crop has a server-side path.

## Estimate

S for the PR itself. M if it becomes a vendored fork, mostly packaging.

title: flatten/1 bakes /AP and ignores /V — a value-only fill flattens to empty
description:
## Why

ADR 0003. Two facts that combine badly:
- PDFium form-field setter writes /V but never regenerates /AP.
- ex_pdfium flatten/1 and flatten_page/2 bake the /AP appearance stream and ignore /V entirely.

So the obvious headless fill route — write /V plus /NeedAppearances true — flattens to the OLD or EMPTY appearance and silently discards the value the user typed. Errors should never pass silently; this one does, and it lands in the fill-then-flatten pipeline Phase 7 depends on.

## Do

1. Hard rule, documented in §9: any /V write MUST also write /AP before the document is flattened or rasterised by anything other than render_page/3.
2. Quire.Pdf.AcroForm owns appearance-stream generation — font metrics plus content-stream emission, NOT a dictionary write. Estimate accordingly.
3. Record FPDFAnnot_SetAP as the fork alternative so the choice is deliberate.
4. Mark T-123 flatten cell as partial ("/AP-only") in the plan.
5. Test: fill a text field headlessly, flatten, rasterise, and assert the value is visible.

## Done when

- The fill-flatten-rasterise round trip preserves the typed value.

## Estimate

M — appearance-stream generation is the real work.

title: /AcroForm and /Outlines do not survive append/2 and extract_pages/2
description:
## Why

ADR 0003. ex_pdfium append/2 (merge) and extract_pages/2 (split) drop the document /AcroForm and /Outlines while leaving the widget annotations behind. The output LOOKS like a form and is not one — fields render but nothing is fillable.

This makes T-081 Merge documented options unimplementable as written: plan3.md specifies "continue page numbering, keep/flatten bookmarks, keep/discard forms", and "keep forms" cannot be done through append/2.

## Do

1. Quire.Pdf.AcroForm re-attaches /AcroForm /Fields after any page import, over the Quire.Pdf object model.
2. Same for /Outlines via Quire.Pdf.Outline.
3. Amend the T-081 row from "bookmark handling" to "bookmark AND form handling".
4. Any merge/split step upstream of Gate 7 must re-attach.
5. Re-confirm against a real Acrobat-produced form in the §13 corpus — the finding was measured on hand-built fixtures.

## Done when

- Merge with "keep forms" produces a document whose fields are still fillable in Acrobat.

## Estimate

S, once Quire.Pdf exists. Blocked on it.

title: Crop-origin coordinate frame: spatial results are MediaBox, render is CropBox
description:
## Why

ADR 0003. On a page with a non-zero-origin CropBox, every spatial result ex_pdfium returns — text, search rects, annotation bounds, image bounds, link bounds — is in the **MediaBox** frame, while render_page/3 rasterises the **CropBox** region. ExPdfium.bounds_to_pixels/3, the library own documented bridge, does not reconcile them.

Symptom: a search highlight, text-layer overlay or annotation lands offset from what the user sees, on any cropped page. Gate 2 grades on non-zero-origin crop and would have passed it as "a read, satisfied by page_info/2" — it is not.

## Do

1. Quire.Render.Pdfium owns its own PDF-points -> raster-pixel conversion instead of calling ExPdfium.bounds_to_pixels/3. Subtract boxes.crop, falling back to boxes.media when crop is nil (PDFium does NOT fall back on its own), and compose the page /Rotate.
2. Add a crop_nonzero_origin.pdf fixture to the §13 corpus (T-016).
3. Test: a rect from search_text/4 lands inside the rendered bitmap.
4. Make it a Gate 2 exit criterion.

## Done when

- The fixture test passes and is wired into Gate 2.

## Estimate

XS-S for the conversion; the fixture and test are the bulk.

title: Quire.Pdf: Rustler NIF over lopdf for the PDF object model
description:
## Why

ADR 0003 (docs/adr/0003-pdfium-capability-map.md). Four planned modules — Quire.Compose, Quire.PdfA, Quire.SecurityHandler, Quire.Pades — all assume the ability to read and write raw PDF structure. Nothing owned it, and the cost never appeared in any task row, so anyone scheduling from the plan under-books by 1-2 weeks.

PDFium cannot supply it: outline write and linearizing save are absent from PDFium public C API entirely (verified against the vendored headers in pdfium-render 0.8.37), so "patch the MIT fork" does not reach them.

## Decision

Rustler NIF over `lopdf` 0.44.0 (MIT), not a pure-Elixir parser. §3.4 bans external *processes*, not native code — this is the same shape as ex_pdfium and vix, both already in the tree. mise.toml pins rust 1.90; lopdf needs 1.85+.

Verified capabilities (docs.rs/lopdf/latest):
- Document::load / save / save_modern
- catalog and arbitrary dictionary/object modification
- IncrementalDocument — append to original bytes (needed by pdf-17l, preserve signatures)
- SaveOptions::use_object_streams(true) + use_xref_streams(true) — documented 11-61% size reduction, which is the T-083 Compress rewrite
- Bookmark / Outline with add_bookmark() and build_outline() — the outline-write gap
- authenticate_password() — feeds Quire.SecurityHandler

## Do

1. Add the NIF crate under native/quire_pdf. Follow ex_pdfium native/ layout.
2. EVERY NIF must be `#[rustler::nif(schedule = "DirtyCpu")]` — §7.3/T-021 rule, and ex_pdfium is 45/45 compliant as the reference.
3. Surface: open/1, save/2, incremental_save/2, catalog/1, get_object/2, set_object/3, outline read+write, object-stream/xref-stream save options.
4. Decide artefact strategy: rustler_precompiled with our own release matrix, or build-from-source. A from-source ex_pdfium NIF build measures 13.85s, so from-source is tolerable for developers but breaks the "no Rust toolchain" property T-003 established. Record the choice in an ADR.
5. Widen Quire.Compose charter in plan3.md beyond "content-stream generation".

## Done when

- Quire.Pdf opens, mutates and saves a fixture-corpus PDF with an incremental update that Acrobat accepts.
- All NIFs are DirtyCpu and T-021-style verification is recorded.

## Estimate

M-L. Smaller than the 1-2 week pure-Elixir alternative because lopdf does the parsing, but the NIF surface, the DirtyCpu audit and the artefact strategy are real work.
close_reason: Built and committed in 9b02783. 8 NIFs, all DirtyCpu (8/8): open, open_file, page_count, save, save_with (object+xref streams), incremental_save, outline, set_outline. 131 tests pass; tests cross-validate output against PDFium as an independent parser. clippy, rustfmt, mix format and --warnings-as-errors all clean; doctor green after moving the rust pin to 1.91 (rustler 0.38.0 MSRV, cargo hard-refuses below it). Items 3, 4 and 5 spun out rather than dropped: catalog/get_object/set_object -> pdf-yjpc (which now blocks pdf-v6sf), artefact strategy ADR -> pdf-4ymp, Compose charter widening -> folded into pdf-cq1s. Also found and filed: outline/1 returns page: nil for named destinations (pdf-nif4), which LaTeX and Word use heavily. 'Acrobat accepts the incremental update' remains UNVERIFIED — no Acrobat here; PDFium was substituted, and lopdf's incremental writer emits a second %PDF header which stricter readers may reject.

title: Amend Appendix A and D: phantom package, wrong PDFium version, stale requirements
description:
## Why

T-003 pinned mix.exs against the live Hex registry and found Appendix A / Appendix D wrong in several places. mix.exs and docs/adr/0001-native-nif-artefacts.md now record the truth; the plan still does not.

## Do

**Delete the phantom package.** `tesseract_elixir` has never been published to Hex. Remove, do not version-correct, the rows at roughly: §3.3:299, §3.3:319, §3.5:382, T-003:2228, T-019:2244, Appendix A:2624, Appendix D:2738. Replace with a pointer to pdf-tuj and the image_ocr / tesserax candidates. §3.1 also justifies `rustler` partly with "the Tesseract NIF" — that justification is void; rustler is retained only for the EXPDFIUM_BUILD=1 fallback and Tauri.

**Correct the PDFium facts.** Appendix D and §3.3:298 claim PDFium 151.0.7891.0 and pdfium-render 0.9.3. ex_pdfium 0.5.1 actually bundles PDFium 144.0.7543.0 and pdfium-render =0.8.37. Also correct §3.3s capability list — outline, box manipulation and save are read-only, and form filling has no backing NIF (see pdf-ryz).

**Amend the stale version requirements** to what T-003 actually pinned:

| Appendix A says | Reality | Note |
|---|---|---|
| gettext ~> 0.26 | ~> 1.0 | gettext 1.0 shipped; Appendix A predates it |
| phoenix_ecto ~> 4.6 | ~> 4.7 | |
| telemetry_poller ~> 1.1 | ~> 1.3 | |
| dns_cluster ~> 0.1 | ~> 0.2.0 | generator bound is tighter and correct |
| phoenix_live_reload ~> 1.5 | ~> 1.6 | |
| oban ~> 2.18 | ~> 2.23 | |
| saxy ~> 1.x | ~> 1.6 | `~> 1.x` is not valid Mix syntax and raises Version.InvalidRequirementError |
| uniq ~> 0.6 | DELETE the row | pdf-qy6h closed: stock Ecto.UUID v7 |
| vix + image "pin at adoption (T-019)" | == 0.40.0 / ~> 0.72.0, pinned in T-003 | ownership moved; nothing about either was still open |
| (absent) | ecto ~> 3.14.1 | declared explicitly for UUID v7 helpers |
| (absent) | rustler_precompiled ~> 0.8.4 | performs the ex_pdfium download |
| (absent) | bcrypt_elixir ~> 3.3 | added by phx.gen.auth in T-200 |

**Add the missing transitive rows** to the Appendix D licence table: yaml_elixir (MIT), yamerl (BSD-2-Clause, non-SPDX string), bunt (MIT), erlex (Apache-2.0), deep_merge (MIT), statistex (MIT), comeonin (BSD-3-Clause), color (Apache-2.0), sweet_xml (MIT).

## Done when

- Appendix A and D match `mix.lock`, and no row names a package that does not exist.

## Notes

The libvips LGPLv3 corrections are tracked in their own issue — do not fold them in here.

title: ex_pdfium serialises every call behind a process-wide mutex; §7.2 assumes parallel render
description:
## Why

Found reading ex_pdfium 0.5.1 source during T-003. The NIF holds a global `PDFIUM_LOCK` mutex that serialises **every** PDFium call across the whole VM.

§7.2 and §7.5 size Oban render queues from performance cores (T-015, pdf-r4p) and assume render workers run in parallel. With this lock, effective PDFium parallelism is **1**, regardless of queue width — extra workers will contend on the mutex rather than doing work. The 500-page render benchmark (T-056) and the Gate 2 performance bar were both set without knowing this.

Note this is orthogonal to dirty schedulers: all 45 NIFs are correctly DirtyCpu, so the BEAM schedulers are not blocked. The constraint is throughput, not scheduler health.

## Do

1. Confirm the lock scope by reading native/ex_pdfium/src/lib.rs (search PDFIUM_LOCK) — establish whether it guards all entry points or only document open/close.
2. Re-derive the T-015 render queue width. A queue of 8 against a lock of 1 is worse than a queue of 1: it adds contention and memory pressure for no throughput.
3. Decide the mitigation. Options: accept serialisation and size the queue to 1-2; fork ex_pdfium (MIT) to use per-document locks if PDFium is actually thread-safe per-instance; or run several BEAM nodes. PDFium upstream is NOT thread-safe globally, so the lock may be correct and the plan simply wrong.
4. Feed the answer into T-056 benchmark expectations and the Gate 2 bar.

## Done when

- §7.2 states the real concurrency limit and T-015 queue sizing reflects it.

title: libvips in vix is LGPLv3 and statically combined, not LGPL-2.1 dynamically linked
description:
## Why

Found by adversarial licence verification during T-003. plan3.md states in three places (roughly :300, :383, :2740) that libvips is **LGPL-2.1, dynamically linked**, and §3.5 mitigates with "Dynamic linking only, do not modify or statically link. Precompiled vix artefacts satisfy this as shipped."

Both halves of that are factually wrong about the artefact actually shipped:

1. **The licence is LGPL-3.0-or-later, not 2.1.** Upstream libvips is LGPL-2.1-or-later, but the sharp-libvips build that vix bundles conveys it under v3. This is not an "or later" pedantry — the distributor has already elected v3.
2. **It is statically combined, not dynamically linked.** `vix.so` does link dynamically against `libvips-cpp.8.18.3.dylib`, but that dylib is itself a Combined Work statically incorporating **eight LGPLv3 libraries plus MPL-2.0 cairo** — none of which appear anywhere in the plan licence tables.

## Why it matters

LGPLv3 §4 inherits GPLv3 §6 Installation Information / anti-tivoisation. A static combination triggers the §4(d)(0) shared-library or §4(d)(1) suitable-object-code relink duty. The plan currently assumes that duty away. This lands squarely on:

- **§12 Tauri desktop packaging** — shipping a signed, sealed .app bundle containing statically-combined LGPLv3 code is exactly the case §4 governs.
- **T-005 licence scanner** (§3.5) — a scanner keyed on the substring "GPL" will now fire on nine LGPLv3 rows. It needs an explicit LGPL-3.0 allow-entry, not the LGPL-2.1 one the plan implies.
- **T-180 attribution** — the obligation set is larger than recorded.

Also found: `yamerl` reports its Hex licence as the non-SPDX string `BSD 2-Clause` (spaces, not hyphens), which an SPDX matcher will not match. Per §3.5, a scanner that cannot parse a licence field must report unknown, not clean.

## Do

1. Correct the three plan3.md rows to `LGPL-3.0-or-later`, and replace the single libvips row with one row per copyleft component actually inside the dylib (8 x LGPL-3.0 + cairo MPL-2.0). Add MPL-2.0 to the weak-copyleft table.
2. Rewrite the §3.5 mitigation — "dynamic linking only" is not what ships.
3. Decide, before §12: accept the LGPLv3 relink duty for the desktop build, or replace/rebuild vix against a v2.1 libvips.
4. Give T-005 an explicit LGPL-3.0 allow-entry and a non-SPDX normalisation step.

## Done when

- plan3.md licence tables match what `otool -L` and the artefact contents actually show.
- The §12 packaging decision is recorded.

## Notes

No GPL or AGPL dependency exists — verified across all 44 Hex deps, all Apache-2.0 / MIT / BSD / ISC. The Appendix E gate PASSES. This issue is about copyleft *obligations* being understated, not about a banned licence.

title: Amend pdf-7hy: stock Ecto.UUID v7 makes the uniq dependency unnecessary
description:
## Why

plan3.md:643 and §3.7 mandate `Uniq.UUID.uuid7/0`, and pdf-7hy builds `Quire.Schema.__using__` around it. That was true when the plan was written; it is not true now.

Verified during T-200 (phx.gen.auth): mix.lock pins ecto 3.14.1, and deps/ecto/lib/ecto/uuid.ex:14-17 documents `@primary_key {:id, Ecto.UUID, autogenerate: [version: 7]}` verbatim. Both generated schemas now use it and produce genuine v7 ids — confirmed empirically on the changeset path AND the insert_all path.

The subtlety worth keeping: `Ecto.UUID.type()` is `:uuid`, which is NOT in [:id, :binary_id], so ecto/lib/ecto/schema.ex autogenerate_id?/1 returns false and Ecto omits the id from the INSERT — which is what lets the column-level `DEFAULT uuidv7()` fire. Under the plain `:binary_id` primary key, Ecto fills in a v4 even for insert_all, so the database default never fires. Both halves are needed.

`uniq` is not in mix.exs and adding a dependency needs a decision.

## Do

1. Decide: stock `Ecto.UUID` with `autogenerate: [version: 7]` (no new dep), or `uniq` as the plan currently says.
2. If stock, update plan3.md:643 and §3.7, and rewrite pdf-7hy so `Quire.Schema.__using__` emits the Ecto.UUID form.
3. Note that `uniq` with `dump: :raw` would change the Elixir-side representation from hex string to raw binary for every FK, route param and fixture — a real cost that the stock path avoids.

## Done when

- plan3.md and pdf-7hy agree with what lib/quire/accounts/user.ex actually does.
close_reason: Decided and implemented: DROP uniq. Ecto 3.14.1 provides UUID v7 generation (autogenerate: [version: 7], 3.14.0), the helpers to_datetime/1 to_unix/2 version/1 (3.14.1 — hence the ~> 3.14.1 floor in mix.exs, not ~> 3.14), and precision: :monotonic which uniq lacks entirely. An adversarial probe tried to refute this on four fronts and could not. Also found: pdf-7hy's proposed dump: :raw would make the column bytea, breaking both DEFAULT uuidv7() and references(:users, type: :binary_id) in the existing T-200 migration. uniq is absent from mix.exs with a comment; Appendix A's row still needs deleting, tracked in the plan-amendments issue.

title: Assign an owner for stripping daisyUI — §3.1 names T-024, which is EditSession work
description:
## Why

Confirmed during T-001 (pdf-54j): `mix phx.new` 1.8.9 emitted the daisyUI dep (`{:daisyui, github: "saadeghi/daisyui", tag: "v5.5.20", ...}`) plus two `@plugin "daisyui/packages/bundle/daisyui-theme"` blocks in `assets/css/app.css` and daisyUI-classed markup in `core_components.ex` and the layouts — exactly as §3.1 lines 224-230 predicted.

§3.1 says to "budget half a day in T-024" for the removal. But T-024 in the tracker is pdf-56b, `Editing.Operation` modules with `apply/2`, `invert/1` and the journal property test — unrelated Phase 0 work. So the half-day strip has no owner, and §3.1 is explicit that discovering it late (at `phx.gen.auth` time) is the failure mode to avoid.

## Do

1. Decide where the strip lands. Candidates: T-002/T-003 (dep hygiene, before any chrome exists — cheapest, nothing to rewrite yet), or T-026 (pdf-0in, TitleBar) where the bespoke §8 chrome first appears.
2. Correct the T-024 reference in §3.1 of plan3.md to the chosen task.
3. Confirm the same cleanup is scheduled for the `phx.gen.auth` output — that is pdf-aam (P0, run phx.gen.auth in Phase 0), not T-163 as §3.1 states.

## Done when

- The daisyUI dep, the `@plugin` blocks and the daisyUI-classed generated markup have a named owning task.
- plan3.md §3.1 points at that task rather than at T-024.

## Notes

The accent token added in T-001 (`--color-accent` in an `@theme static` block) is independent of daisyUI and survives the strip. Note the `static` keyword is load-bearing: a plain `@theme` block tree-shakes unreferenced tokens out of the compiled CSS.
close_reason: Resolved while doing pdf-aam: the daisyUI strip owner is T-025 (plan3.md:2249 area), not T-024. §3.1 said T-024 and T-163; both were off by one and are now corrected to T-025 and T-200. T-025's row was also widened to cover the six phx.gen.auth templates.

title: Ad-hoc re-sign mix-downloaded tailwind/esbuild binaries in bootstrap and doctor
description:
## Why

Discovered during T-001 (pdf-54j). `mix assets.build` fails on a clean macOS 27 machine with `** (Mix) `mix tailwind quire` exited with 137` (SIGKILL). §3.6.6 anticipates this and prescribes `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <path>` — **that fix is insufficient on this OS version**. The downloaded binary carries `com.apple.provenance` (not `com.apple.quarantine`), which `xattr -c` cannot remove, and `spctl -a` reports `invalid signature (code or signature have been modified)` on the vendor's ad-hoc/linker-signed Mach-O.

The working fix is to re-sign ad hoc after download:

```
codesign --force -s - _build/tailwind-macos-arm64-<ver>
```

`xattr -cr` alone did not help and may itself invalidate an ad-hoc signature.

## Do

1. Correct §3.6.6 of plan3.md: keep the quarantine note, add the `com.apple.provenance` / `codesign --force -s -` case as the actual remedy.
2. Wire the re-sign into T-002 (pdf-l0q) bootstrap so `mix assets.setup` is followed by a re-sign step for every mix-downloaded binary (tailwind, esbuild, and later any precompiled NIF artefact).
3. Add a `mise run doctor` assertion that each downloaded binary executes (`--help` exits 0), so Gate 0 catches a regression on a clean checkout rather than at first asset build.

## Done when

- A fresh clone on a second machine runs `mix assets.build` successfully with no manual codesign step.
- `mise run doctor` fails loudly if a downloaded binary is killed by Gatekeeper.
close_reason: Implemented in T-002: mise run assets:resign (codesign --force --sign -), called from mise run setup; mise run doctor asserts every downloaded binary executes; plan3.md §3.6.6 corrected with the com.apple.provenance case.

title: Implement or drop the Trial-tier watermark-on-export policy
description:
## Why
F-14 (major). §11.2 (plan3.md:1937) grants Trial users "Everything, watermarked output on export", and no task in §15 implements it - T-165 (2500) is expiry only and Gate 12 (2509-2511) tests deny-gating only. "Export" is never defined: if Save counts, a trial user's original file is overwritten with a watermarked copy (1866); if not, the watermark is bypassed by Save-then-open. It also contradicts the same tier's features - watermarking after a PAdES signature invalidates it (1678), before it makes the trial mark permanent in a countersigned contract, and an extra layer invalidates the PDF/A conformance report (1507). `allows?/2` is boolean (1942) and cannot express "allowed but degraded"; `licenses` (658-662) carries only `tier`.

## Do
1. Decide and record: which outputs count as export (recommended: downloads, conversions, ZIPs and print PDFs - not Save to the user's own library), and that signing and PDF/A are exempt rather than watermarked.
2. If keeping it: add a policy call beside `allows?/2` (e.g. `output_policy/2`) and apply it at the single export seam, reusing the `Compose` stamping already built for T-096.
3. If dropping it: delete the cell from §11.2 and state that the trial is time-limited only.
4. Settle the export seam by Phase 4 so the conversion paths are built with the hook in place.

## Done when
- [ ] §11.2 either defines export precisely or no longer promises a watermark
- [ ] If kept: every export path routes through one policy function, with a test per path
- [ ] Test: a trial user's signed output validates in Acrobat, i.e. signing is exempt
- [ ] Gate 12 asserts the chosen behaviour

title: Decide the Windows/Linux build-host story or scope Gate 13 to macOS
description:
## Why
F-13 (major). Gate 13 requires the app to "build and run on all three platforms" (plan3.md:2533-2535) via T-183 (Windows MSI/NSIS) and T-184 (deb + AppImage), but the plan supplies no host that can produce them: target is macOS arm64 only (387-388), containers are banned (158-161), there is no CI (2194), the Brewfile and mise.toml are macOS-only (2601-2640), and T-180 verifies with `otool -L` only (2526). Tauri does not cross-compile, and `mix release` embeds a host-built ERTS into `bundle.resources` (1985-1987), so each platform needs its own OTP/Elixir build. The three NIFs also need `rustler_precompiled` artefacts for msvc and linux-gnu that T-003 never checks. R-11 (2670) already assumes a Linux build exists.

## Do
1. Choose (a): scope Gate 13 to macOS for v1, move T-183/T-184 to a named post-1.0 phase, and update §12's "the two platforms you have not been developing on" (1975) and R-11 to match. Recommended - it makes a 1.5-week phase honest.
2. Or choose (b): name real Windows and Linux build machines in the reproducibility contract, add per-platform `mise.toml` tool sets, extend T-003 to verify `rustler_precompiled` artefacts for each target triple, and run one `mix release` per host.
3. Either way extend T-180 beyond `otool -L` to the `ldd` and `dumpbin /dependents` equivalents for whichever platforms ship.
4. Record the decision in an ADR before Phase 13 starts - ideally during Phase 0.

## Done when
- [ ] Gate 13's wording matches the platforms the project can actually build
- [ ] If (b): each named build host is in the toolchain contract and has produced one green build
- [ ] T-003 checks precompiled NIF artefacts for every shipping target triple
- [ ] R-11 and §12 no longer assume a build host that does not exist

title: Define the PAdES trust model and generate a test CA
description:
## Why
FD2-02 (major). Gate 8 (plan3.md:2431-2432) grades on "a signature applied here validates **in Acrobat**, and every fixture signature validates **here**", and the plan never names a trust anchor, a root store or a test CA. Greps for `trust`, `cacert`, `CRL`, `OCSP` return nothing relevant: 303 and 1678 say "verify the chain" with no anchor; 1748 descopes *becoming* a QTSP, the opposite; 1954 is the user's own keys. T-131's acceptance says only "verifies the certificate chain natively".

Outbound: Acrobat calls a signature valid only when the signer chains to AATL/EUTL or to Trusted Identities, so a self-signed test certificate renders "validity is UNKNOWN" — implying either an AATL purchase (nowhere in Appendix B/D) or a manual trust import T-138 never records. Inbound: `signed_pades.pdf` (2102) has no stated provenance, and `:public_key.cacerts_get/0` is the OS **TLS** store, a different population from document-signing CAs. `validation_status` is persisted and shown to the user, so choosing wrong declares real contracts untrusted, or trusts everything.

## Do
1. Add a paragraph to §9.7 naming the trust model: a configured PEM bundle (`config :quire, :pades_trust_anchors`) plus a user-managed anchor list, and say whether the OS TLS store seeds it.
2. Report "not trusted" as a `validation_status` distinct from "cryptographically invalid".
3. Generate a self-signed test CA + leaf into `test/support/pki/`, use it for app-produced fixtures, and document the one-time Acrobat "add to Trusted Identities" step so T-138's cross-check is reproducible.
4. Restate Gate 8 as "validates in Acrobat **with the test CA imported as a trusted identity**".

## Done when
- [ ] §9.7 names the anchor source and T-131 consults it
- [ ] A test CA exists in the repo and app-produced signatures chain to it
- [ ] Untrusted-but-valid and invalid signatures are distinguishable in the Signatures panel
- [ ] Gate 8's wording is achievable without buying an AATL certificate

title: Preserve existing signatures on save (incremental update or refuse)
description:
## Why
F-08 (major). Save uploads a full client-side re-serialisation of the document (plan3.md:1238-1242) - `saveDocument()` for pdf.js-native types and `@cantoo/pdf-lib` for the rest (1643-1645). Both rewrite the whole file, so any existing PAdES signature's `/ByteRange` is destroyed. §9.7 (1678) and §9.9 (1741-1743) assume post-signature changes arrive as appended incremental updates, and signed documents are a normal state - `signed_pades.pdf` is in the corpus and E-Sign appends a completion signature. The string "incremental" appears nowhere in 2724 lines. Gate 8 (2429-2432) only tests signing, never annotate-then-save-then-revalidate, so this ships invisibly.

## Do
1. Detect signatures on the current revision (a structural `/ByteRange` + `/Sig` scan is enough before Phase 8; use `Pades` validation once it exists).
2. On a signed document, either refuse client-side re-serialisation with a clear explanation and route the edit through a server-side incremental (append-only) writer, or warn unmissably that saving will invalidate N signatures and require confirmation.
3. State in §7.4 which save path is incremental and which is not.
4. Add annotate -> Save -> re-validate to Gate 6 and Gate 8.

## Done when
- [ ] Test: annotate `signed_pades.pdf`, Save, re-open - the original signature still validates, or the user was explicitly warned and consented
- [ ] Test: the completed E-Sign document survives a subsequent comment without failing its own difference analysis
- [ ] §7.4 documents the incremental save path
- [ ] Gate 6 and Gate 8 include the annotate-after-sign case

title: Remap page_index in all five sidecar tables for every page.* op
description:
## Why
F-04 (major, data-leak class). `annotations` (plan3.md:723), `text_edits` (736), `form_fields` (745), `redactions` (761) and `esign_fields` (782) all store an absolute `page_index` with no `revision_id`, while §7.4's ten `page.*` ops (1192) renumber pages. Highlight page 5, delete page 2, and the highlight is on the wrong page - in the table, in the Comments panel and in every export. A drifted `redactions` row is the serious one: the user applies a redaction believing it covers the SSN. The words "remap", "renumber" and "page_uid" appear nowhere in the document, and Gate 3 (2298-2299) is satisfied by a document whose sidecar rows have all silently drifted.

## Do
1. Pick one: (a) add `document_pages.page_uid`, stable across revisions, carried by the page-import splice, and make `page_index` a derived lookup; or (b) make every `page.*` op's `apply/2` and `invert/1` rewrite the affected indices in all five tables in the same transaction.
2. Cover insert, delete, move, reverse, replace and split/merge inflows.
3. Add the assertion to Gate 3 and re-check it before T-134 (Apply redaction) ships.

## Done when
- [ ] Test: with a redaction mark on page 5, deleting page 2 leaves the mark covering the same content
- [ ] Test: the same for an annotation, a form field, a text edit and an esign field
- [ ] Test: undo of each page op restores the original indices
- [ ] Gate 3 asserts sidecar-table integrity after a reorder-and-undo sequence

description:

title: T-059: Build the Page tab thumbnail workspace grid
description:
## Task

title: Write the feature-key catalogue mapping every control to a tier
description:
## Why
F-C203 (major). §11.2 (plan3.md:1935-1945) specifies `allows?(user, :feature_key)` and a `<.gated>` component against a four-row prose table whose feature domain is never enumerated. Whole areas fall outside every row: the **entire Page tab** (1519-1549 — Insert, Extract, Replace, Move, Reverse, Background, Size, Margin, Export images, Page crop, Remove crop, Rotate, Delete), plus Compare (1660), Export comments (1661), PDF/A, PDF to Image and PDF to TXT/RTF/HTML (1506-1510). T-164 (2499) implements the mechanism and its acceptance is "`allows?/2` returns the §11.2 table's tier->feature mapping" — a mapping that does not exist for ~40 controls shipped in Phases 3-11. Gate 12's bar (2509-2510) is unassessable for a `:transform` worker driven from the Page tab because no tier claims it. Separately, the MenuBar renders all 11 tabs unconditionally (2231) and §8.2's only non-enabled state is per-button opacity (1364-1365), so an unlicensed *tab* has no defined destination.

## Do
1. Add a table to §11.2 mapping every §9 and §10 control to exactly one `:feature_key`, and every key to a minimum tier — including an explicit decision for the Page tab.
2. State the whole-tab treatment. Recommended: the tab stays visible and its ribbon renders behind the upsell overlay, preserving parity with the persistent `Activate now`.
3. Land this before Phase 3 builds the Page tab, so `<.gated>` is applied as controls are written rather than retrofitted across ~40 controls times three enforcement points.
4. Have each phase's gate assert its own tab's keys exist and deny correctly at the worker level.

## Done when
- [ ] Every control in §9 and §10 maps to exactly one feature key, checked by a test that walks the ribbon definitions
- [ ] Every key has a minimum tier and a unit test per tier
- [ ] The unlicensed-tab treatment is specified once and implemented once
- [ ] Gates 3 through 11 each assert their tab's gating

title: Carry revision-scoped page and text caches forward on server ops
description:
## Why
F-05 (major). `document_pages` and `document_page_text` are keyed by `revision_id` (plan3.md:682-689) and are populated only by the §10.3 ingest pipeline (1901-1904). The §7.4 server-op flow (1219-1227) advances `documents.current_revision_id` without re-deriving either, so after any rotate/merge/compress/OCR/redact the Thumbnails panel (T-046) and the Recent cards (1844) go blank and the server-side search fallback (T-048) returns zero hits - silently, because an empty index looks like no matches. Gate 2's search assertion passes at ingest and regresses the first time anyone edits. Undo makes it worse: `{:restore_revision, id}` points back at an old revision, so the caches must be maintained per revision, not merely refreshed.

## Do
1. Add step 3.5 to §7.4's server-op flow: the worker MUST populate `document_pages` for the new revision and enqueue thumbnail + text refresh for the changed page range only.
2. Make page-preserving ops (crop, rotate, background, metadata) copy the parent revision's rows instead of re-rendering.
3. Implement it once in the T-061 splice primitive so every later op inherits it.
4. State the incremental rule explicitly - re-thumbnailing 500 pages at <= 100 ms/page (2128) is ~50 s of queue work per op with `render: 4`.

## Done when
- [ ] After a page rotate on `500_pages.pdf`, the thumbnails panel is populated and only the changed pages were re-rendered
- [ ] After OCR, the server search fallback returns hits for the new revision
- [ ] Undo restores the previous revision and its caches are still present
- [ ] Gate 3 asserts thumbnails and server search still work after a transform

title: Gate 3: 200-page reorder, crop, re-crop with undo; Acrobat-clean
description:
## Acceptance gate

## Verify

title: Name an owner for embedded-file add/remove and re-scope T-049
description:
## Why
G-04 (major). §3.3's PDFium row grants "attachment enumeration/**extraction**" (plan3.md:297) and §7.3's mutation surface is `import_pages/...`, `new_document/...`, `add_page_objects/...`, `save/...` (1144-1145). Neither writes `/Names/EmbeddedFiles`. Yet T-049 (2264, **Phase 2**) promises an Attachments panel with "add, remove", and §7.4's op catalogue (1189-1195) has no attachment kind — the nearest is `annot.add` with `annotations.kind :attachment` (725), which is a `/FileAttachment` annotation, a different PDF structure. Phase 2 also has no client mutation library: `DocMutateHook` is T-088, **Phase 5**. §9.6 line 1654 puts `/FileAttachment` authoring in T-107, **Phase 6**. By §3.3's own rule (292-293) an unlisted capability means the feature's design is wrong — the same class as F-C205's missing font pipeline. x02 audits what §3.3 *claims*, not what §9 *needs*, so it does not catch this.

## Do
1. Decide the owner: extend the `Render` mutation surface with `add_embedded_file/remove_embedded_file` if `ex_pdfium` exposes it, or assign `/Names/EmbeddedFiles` writing to `Quire.Compose` alongside x02's other write-side orphans.
2. Add `attach.add` / `attach.delete` op kinds to §7.4 with inverses, or route both through `{:restore_revision, id}` as server ops.
3. Re-scope T-049 to list / preview / extract in Phase 2 and move add / remove to Phase 6 beside T-107, so no task promises mutation before a mutation path exists.
4. Fold the demand-side sweep into x02: for every §9 control, check the capability it needs is on §3.3's table.

## Done when
- [ ] §3.3 line 297 and §7.3 lines 1144-1145 name an owner for embedded-file writing, or the feature is cut and the plan says so
- [ ] T-049's Phase-2 acceptance no longer claims add/remove
- [ ] Adding then undoing an attachment round-trips through the journal, tested on `with_attachments.pdf`
- [ ] x02's audit covers demand as well as supply
notes:
DECISION: Embedded file add/remove ownership assigned to Phase 6 (Comment tab, alongside T-107 /FileAttachment annotations). Implementation through DocMutateHook/mutate.js using @cantoo/pdf-lib — same pipeline as other client-side mutations.

RATIONALE: ex_pdfium has no write API for embedded files (§3.3 line 297: read-only for attachments). Quire.Compose is content-stream/appearance-stream only — out of scope. @cantoo/pdf-lib (already in use by mutate.js/T-088) can manipulate any PDF structure including /Names/EmbeddedFiles.

T-049 re-scoped: list/preview/extract stays in Phase 2 (closed). Add/remove deferred to Phase 6. attach.add/attach.delete op kinds to be added alongside annot.add/annot.delete when Phase 6 implements them.

title: Replace the geometry round-trip test with a JS-Elixir differential
description:
## Why
F-11 (major). §14.3 mandates "a round-trip `css -> pdf -> css` is the identity within 0.01 pt" (plan3.md:2164-2165), which is true for any invertible function including a wrong one - it passes on day one and catches none of the four mismatches the section lists. Worse, §14.3 requires the same maths twice, in `geometry.js` and "a matching Elixir module" (2149-2150), and a round trip inside either cannot detect that the two have diverged - which is the actual risk of the design. This tautology is R-09's only named mitigation (2668) besides the "single-source module" §14.3 itself contradicts. The tolerance unit is also wrong: the round trip ends in CSS px, not pt.

## Do
1. Keep the round-trip test as a cheap sanity check but stop treating it as the mitigation.
2. Add a differential test: generate random (page size, /Rotate, CropBox, scale, point) tuples, run them through pdf.js's `PageViewport.convertToPdfPoint`/`convertToViewportPoint` in headless Chromium (the Playwright harness) and through the Elixir twin, and assert agreement within 0.01 pt in PDF space.
3. Add fixture assertions against known-good coordinates on `cropped_nonzero_origin.pdf` and `rotated_pages.pdf`.
4. Update R-09's mitigation column to name the differential test.

## Done when
- [ ] A differential test compares JS and Elixir over >= 1000 random tuples and fails on divergence
- [ ] Fixture assertions cover rotation 90/180/270 and a non-zero-origin CropBox
- [ ] Deliberately breaking one implementation makes the suite red
- [ ] §14.3 and R-09 describe the differential test, not the round trip

title: Rebuild the server search fallback as pre-filter plus offset scan
description:
## Why
F-10 (major). T-048 (plan3.md:2263) says the two search paths "must present identically" and Gate 2 grades on it (2278-2279), but the index is `to_tsvector('simple', content)` (688). The `simple` dictionary lower-cases and tokenises, so: match case has no server implementation; whole word is the server's only mode; `form` cannot match `information`, which `PDFFindController` hits by default; and hyphenation/ligatures/punctuation-joined tokens break. Worse, a tsvector stores lexeme ordinals, not character offsets into `content`, so there is nothing to "map hits back to page + rect via the stored spans" with. §5.2's rationale (701-704) conflates "no stemming" with "matches literally".

## Do
1. Make the server path two-stage: use the GIN/tsvector index only as a page pre-filter (`search @@ websearch_to_tsquery(...)`), then run in Elixir the same normalisation + substring scan the client uses over that page's `content` to get character offsets.
2. Map offsets -> `spans` -> page + rect, sharing the normalisation rules with the client so results are comparable.
3. Support match-case and whole-word as scan-level flags.
4. Restate Gate 2's bar as "identical hit sets on `500_pages.pdf` for case-sensitive, case-insensitive and whole-word queries", and fix §5.2's rationale text.

## Done when
- [ ] Server search returns page + rect for every hit, not just page
- [ ] Test: `form` matches inside `information` on both paths
- [ ] Test: match-case on and off give the same hit sets on both paths
- [ ] Gate 2 asserts identical hit sets across all three toggle combinations

title: Specify share-link schema, public route and revocation surface
description:
## Why
G-03 (major). §8.2 (plan3.md:1346-1350) commits the workspace to a "share" control creating "an expiring, optionally password-protected view/comment link, with a revocation list in Settings", and says it is in scope (T-198, 2241, **Phase 1**). Nothing behind it exists: §5 (647-828) has no share table; §6's web tree (960-967) has `esign/sign_live.ex` and `esign_controller.ex` and no share equivalent; §11.3's eight named settings tabs (1952-1956) contain no revocation list, and T-166 renders that screen in **Phase 12**. The plan sets a clear standard for its other public token route — §9.9 lines 1732-1736: "single-purpose, expiring, and rate-limited" — and share links inherit none of it. "Comment" access also has no identity model: `annotations.author` is free text (728) but `annotation_replies.user_id` is a FK to `users` (732), so an anonymous commenter cannot reply. This is the schema/route half; FD2-04 separately covers T-198's phase placement.

## Do
1. Add `share_links` to §5 and to T-007: `document_id`, `revision_id`, `token`, `scope (:view | :comment)`, `password_hash`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`, `created_by`, `last_accessed_at`.
2. Specify `/share/:token` as a public LiveView under §9.9's token rules (single-purpose, expiring, rate-limited), and state that §12.2's origin checking is not weakened for it.
3. Decide the anonymous-commenter model: either require a display name stored on the annotation and forbid replies, or issue a lightweight guest identity.
4. Add "Sharing (active links, revoke)" to §11.3's tab list so T-166 has somewhere to render it.
5. Note in §1.2 that share links, like E-Sign, need the tunnel to be exercised at all.

## Done when
- [ ] `share_links` exists in §5 and in T-007's migration
- [ ] A revoked or expired token returns a clear refusal, asserted by a test
- [ ] A password-protected link rejects a wrong password and rate-limits attempts
- [ ] The revocation list has a home in §11.3 and T-166 renders it

title: Vendor pdf.sandbox.mjs and wire PDFScriptingManager
description:
## Why
G-02 (major). Two features require pdf.js's scripting sandbox and no task delivers it. §9.5 (plan3.md:1632-1633) says a Run JavaScript action must be sandboxed "in the viewer via pdf.js's `PDFScriptingManager` + `pdf.sandbox.mjs`", and §3.2 line 261 lists `PDFScriptingManager` among the viewer components. But T-040 (2255) copies only `cmaps/`, `standard_fonts/`, `iccs/`, `wasm/`, and T-042 (2257) wraps only `PDFViewer` + `EventBus` + `PDFLinkService`. T-093's own acceptance requires JS actions to run "only through `PDFScriptingManager` + `pdf.sandbox.mjs`" — an asset no task copies into `priv/static`.

The bigger consequence is Forms: §9.8 line 1698 gives text fields "format (number/date/currency/percentage/custom), validation, calculation" and line 1714 requires "calculated fields recompute". Those are `/AA` JavaScript actions. Gate 7's bar is Acrobat + Chrome (2403-2404), both of which have their own JS engines, so the gate passes while this product's viewer shows stale or unformatted values. T-120 and T-126 defer every calculation assertion to Acrobat.

## Do
1. Add `pdf.sandbox.mjs` (and its wasm/worker companions) to T-040's copy list and to `mise run assets.vendor`.
2. Instantiate `PDFScriptingManager` in `PdfViewerHook`, gated by the same default-off setting as §9.5's Run JavaScript, and pass `sandboxBundleSrc` to `getDocument`.
3. State in §9.8 whether field format/validate/calculate is evaluated in-app (scripting on) or explicitly out of scope, and say so in the field-properties dialog.
4. Add an in-app assertion to T-126, not only an Acrobat one.

## Done when
- [ ] `pdf.sandbox.mjs` is served from `priv/static/vendor/pdfjs/` after a clean `mise run assets.vendor`
- [ ] With scripting enabled, a two-field calculated form authored by T-119/T-120 recomputes **in this app's viewer**
- [ ] With scripting disabled (the default) no JS action is evaluated anywhere, asserted by a test
- [ ] §9.8 states the supported behaviour instead of implying it

title: Implement the View toggle pill as a document-wide read-only mode
description:
## Why
F-C202 (major). §8.2 (plan3.md:1368-1371) mandates a dark **View toggle pill** on the Edit, Comment, Secure, Forms, E-Sign and OCR tabs that "switches the document between **edit and read-only preview**", and tells the implementer to "implement it as a single boolean in `WorkspaceLive` assigns". A whole-file grep for "toggle pill" returns one hit and "read-only preview" one hit. No §15 task owns it: T-026, T-028, T-029, T-030 and T-031 (2229-2234) are the Phase-1 chrome tasks and none mentions it; T-029's spec block cites the line but every one of its acceptance items is about ribbon metrics and `zoom_control`.

Read-only preview is not a boolean. It must suppress the §9.4 floating palette (1570-1571), pdf.js's `annotationEditorMode` (1652), §9.7's redaction marking (1679), §9.8's field placement (1698-1704), §9.5's content-stream path (1591-1596) and §9.10's OCR invocation — six tabs built across Phases 5-10, none of which is told the mode exists. Retrofitting it after the tools exist is exactly the failure plan3.md:2185-2186 warns about.

## Do
1. Add `:view_mode` (`:edit | :preview`) to `WorkspaceLive` assigns and render the pill left of `Activate now` on the six named tabs.
2. Write the contract every later tool must satisfy: floating palettes hidden, `annotationEditorMode = NONE`, every mutating LiveView event rejected server-side (not merely hidden), tools deactivated on flip.
3. State what happens to a tool mid-interaction when the pill flips, and whether `dirty?` (1183) blocks the flip.
4. Add "the pill disables every mutating control on this tab" to Gates 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.

## Done when
- [ ] The pill renders on exactly the six tabs named at line 1369
- [ ] In `:preview`, a hand-crafted mutating LiveView event is rejected server-side, tested per tab
- [ ] Flipping mid-interaction cancels the active tool without losing committed work
- [ ] Gates 5-10 each carry the assertion

title: Add the text-extraction worker that populates document_page_text
description:
## Why
G-01 (major). Nothing writes `document_page_text`. §5.2 says "populate it from the text-layer probe in §10.3 step 5" (plan3.md:699-700), but step 5 only enqueues "a text-layer probe (**does the document have extractable text?**)" (1903-1904) — a boolean, not per-page `content` plus `spans`. §6's worker list (893-903) has `render_worker.ex` and no text worker. T-045 (2260) is the thumbnail half of the same step and has no twin. A grep of all 199 tasks for `document_page_text` returns exactly two: T-006 (the migration, 2195) and T-048 (the consumer, 2263). **Gate 2 grades the server-side fallback on `500_pages.pdf`** (2278-2279). x10 (query shape) and x12 (carry-forward on server ops) both assume the rows already exist, so neither closes this.

## Do
1. Add `Quire.Workers.TextExtractWorker` on the `:render` queue: for each page call `Render.extract_text/2` (§7.3 line 1139), write `document_page_text` rows (`revision_id`, `page_index`, `content`, `spans`) and set `document_pages.has_text`.
2. Enqueue it from §10.3 step 5 alongside the thumbnail job, with the same `unique:` guard as T-045 (§7.5 lines 1288-1293).
3. Report progress through `Workers.Base` and make it idempotent under retry.
4. Split the two jobs explicitly in §10.3 step 5 so "probe" is no longer one word covering two pipelines.
5. Make it the predecessor of x10 and x12.

## Done when
- [ ] After opening `500_pages.pdf`, `document_page_text` has one row per page with non-empty `spans`
- [ ] `document_pages.has_text` is false for `scanned_300dpi.pdf` and drives the "run OCR first" prompt (T-145)
- [ ] Gate 2's server-fallback assertion runs against rows this worker wrote, not against an empty table
- [ ] The worker is idempotent: running it twice produces one row set

title: Add image and text fixtures so the vix and Tesseract NIFs get fuzzed
description:
## Why
FD2-03 (major). §13's corpus (plan3.md:2100-2107) is twenty PDFs plus five Office files. A grep for `.png/.jpe?g/.tiff?/.heic/.webp/.bmp` over 2724 lines returns **zero hits**, and T-016 (2205) mirrors the list exactly.
