A PDF cannot be fed to libvips or Tesseract, so the sweep is unsatisfiable for two of the three NIFs: the implementer narrows it to PDFium (leaving both unfuzzed) or rasterises first, handing them only well-formed PDFium output. That is the path R-07 (2666) is about, over §7.2's "least trusted input path" (331). Seven features take user images (T-073, T-075, T-066, T-080, T-092, T-114, T-143) with no input file in the repo; Gate 4 and Gate 9 grade some of them. Appendix B.3's doctor rows (2650-2651) also assume a test image on every boot.

## Do
1. Add to §13 and T-016: `photo.jpg`, `screenshot.png`, `scan_gray.tiff`, `multipage.tiff`, `transparent.png`, `cmyk.jpg`, `huge_dimensions.png`, `truncated.jpg`, `exif_rotated.jpg`, plus one `.heic` if the pinned vix ships the loader.
2. Add `notes.txt`, `data.csv` and `readme.md` for T-073's direct-to-HTML path.
3. Restate T-020 and T-197 as "every fixture through every NIF **that accepts its type**", with the image set going directly to vix and Tesseract, never via PDFium.

title: Add a signing-credential store with the cloak_ecto at-rest rule
description:
## Why
F-C208 (major). Three sections and one task commit to storing and managing user signing certificates, and §5 defines no table for them. §9.7 (plan3.md:1678): "parse **PKCS#12 keystores** ... Flow: **choose or upload a certificate** -> place the visible field -> sign". §11.1 (1922-1923) gates "managing certificates" behind sudo mode. §11.3 (1954-1955) puts a "certificate store" in Settings -> Security. T-130 (2419) owns the "certificate management UI". But §5.4's `digital_signatures` (764-768) holds only post-hoc metadata and there is no keystore, key or passphrase anywhere in 647-828. Contrast the rule the plan gives for its other stored secret: "Tokens MUST be encrypted at rest (`cloak_ecto` or equivalent)" (828), scoped only to §5.6. With no schema the T-130 implementer invents one mid-Phase-8, and the obvious shortcuts (an unencrypted `Storage` ref; the passphrase in a long-lived assign) are what R-04 (2663) cannot afford. T-129 parses a keystore and never says where it goes.

## Do
1. Add `signing_credentials` to §5.4 and to T-007: `user_id`, `label`, `subject`, `issuer`, `serial`, `not_after`, `keystore_ref` (Storage ref), `passphrase_encrypted`.
2. Put it under the same `cloak_ecto` rule as `cloud_connections`, and say so in §5.4 rather than only in §5.6.
3. State that the passphrase is requested per signature and never persisted in plaintext, and that the assign is zeroed like §9.7 line 1677 requires for document passwords.
4. Point T-130's certificate-management UI and T-166's Settings -> Security tab at this table.

## Done when
- [ ] `signing_credentials` exists in §5.4 and in T-007's migration
- [ ] Keystore bytes live behind a `Storage.Ref` and the passphrase column is Cloak-encrypted, asserted by a test that reads the raw row
- [ ] Signing prompts for the passphrase per signature; no test can find it in a socket assign afterwards
- [ ] Sudo mode gates every mutation of this table (§11.1)

title: Decide Storage key semantics: content-addressed or UUID, not both
description:
## Why
F-06 (major). §7.1 says the filesystem backend's key is "a content-addressed relative path under the data root" (plan3.md:1024-1027) and, fifteen lines later, that keys are `<first2>/<next2>/<uuid>` (1039-1042). These cannot both be true and the choice is not cosmetic. If content-addressed, two revisions with identical bytes share one blob, and T-172's prune (2507) deletes bytes a live revision of another document still references - silent data loss with no refcounting specified anywhere. If UUID-keyed, `document_revisions`'s "content-addressed" comment (676) is false and the `sha256` column (679) is only for integrity. Every later phase builds on whichever T-009 picks.

## Do
1. Pick one and say it once in §7.1. Recommended: UUID-keyed with `sha256` retained for integrity verification and dedup reporting - it keeps retention trivially safe.
2. Strike the contradicting wording from plan3.md:1025 or :1041, and fix the comment at 676.
3. If content-addressing is chosen instead, specify refcounting (or a "delete only when no `document_revisions.storage_ref` references this key" query) as a precondition on T-172, and cover Save-with-no-change, Save as and undo-then-redo in tests.
4. Record the decision in an ADR and reflect it in T-009's test suite.

## Done when
- [ ] §7.1 states exactly one key scheme
- [ ] `StorageCase` asserts the chosen scheme for both adapters
- [ ] T-172 carries the matching deletion precondition
- [ ] Test: writing identical bytes twice behaves as the ADR says (shared blob + refcount, or two blobs)

title: Wire UUID v7 into the schema layer and assert it on inserts
description:
## Why
F-15 (major). T-001 runs `mix phx.new --binary-id` (plan3.md:2190), which emits `@primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}` - and Ecto's `:binary_id` autogenerate is `Ecto.UUID.bingenerate/0`, i.e. UUID **v4**. Only `insert_all` and raw SQL fall through to the column `DEFAULT uuidv7()` (2195). That is exactly the silent mixing §3.7 warns against (504-509) and it defeats the index-locality rationale the design "leans on hardest" for `document_revisions` and `edit_operations` (636-640). It is invisible: both are valid 16-byte UUIDs and every test passes. The document never says to declare a v7 primary key type on the schemas.

## Do
1. Add `Quire.Schema` with a `__using__` macro setting `@primary_key {:id, Uniq.UUID, autogenerate: true, version: 7, dump: :raw}` and `@foreign_key_type Uniq.UUID`.
2. Require every schema to `use Quire.Schema`; add a Credo check or a test that fails on a schema that does not.
3. Keep `DEFAULT uuidv7()` as the backstop and say in §3.7 that `--binary-id` alone yields v4.

## Done when
- [ ] Every Ecto schema uses the shared macro
- [ ] Test: a changeset-inserted row's id has version nibble 7
- [ ] Test: an `insert_all` row's id also has version nibble 7
- [ ] §3.7 and §5 state that `--binary-id` autogenerate is v4 and must be overridden

title: Flush pending client-side edits to a revision before any server op
description:
## Why
F-03 (major). Client ops live only in the browser's copy of the PDF until Save (plan3.md:1238-1241). A server op reads `base_revision_id` from Storage, which does not contain them, and step 4 of the server flow (1219-1227) tells the hook to reload the new revision. Highlight three paragraphs, hit Page > Rotate, and the highlights vanish with no error. `dirty?` is tracked (1183) and never consulted here; grep for "flush" returns nothing. §7.4 calls this "the hardest design problem in the project; get it right in Phase 0" (1177-1178).

## Do
1. In `Editing.apply/2` with `applied_side: :server`, check the journal for unpersisted client ops.
2. If any exist, request the hook's `saveDocument()` bytes, create an intermediate revision from them, and enqueue the Oban job against that revision id.
3. Journal the intermediate revision so undo crosses it correctly (coordinate with x04's chain rules).
4. If the hook cannot answer (closed tab, degraded mode), fail the op with a plain-language message rather than silently discarding edits.

## Done when
- [ ] Test: annotate 3 regions, rotate a page server-side, reload - all 3 annotations are present in the new revision's bytes
- [ ] Test: the same flow with the hook unavailable produces an error, not a silent loss
- [ ] §7.4's server-op flow documents the flush step
- [ ] Gate 0 includes the annotate-then-transform assertion

title: Decide the font pipeline: sources, subsetting, shaping, licensing
description:
## Why
F-C205 (major). Four features need server-side font bytes selected, embedded and (for CJK) subset, and §3.3 — which declares itself "the **complete** server-side engine inventory" (plan3.md:291-293) — assigns that to nobody. Demand: §9.2's PDF/A must "verify/**embed** fonts" (1507); §9.5's page numbers, watermarks, headers/footers and Bates all take a font and are rendered by `Compose` + PDFium page objects (1605-1608); the format bar offers "embedded + standard-14 + **uploaded**" families (1615); §9.11 targets ~60 languages through `Compose` (1787-1788). Supply: the PDFium row (297) lists page-object creation with no font loading; the PdfA row (305) says embedding **verification**, narrower than 1507; the Compose row (306) has no font resource management. Greps: "subsetting" 0, "shaping" 0, "harfbuzz" 0, "bidi" 0, "Noto" 0. The only font assets named anywhere are pdf.js's `standard_fonts/` (251, 2255) — a client-side viewer resource that cannot be embedded into a server-produced PDF. §3.5 (377-383) never considers fonts and T-005's licence scan reads Hex/npm metadata, not bundled data.

## Do
1. Write an ADR: which permissively-licensed families ship as app data; who subsets (a `Compose.Font` over PDFium's font API, or pure-Elixir TTF subsetting); whether complex-script shaping is supported or explicitly refused with a message; storage and licence rules for uploaded user fonts.
2. Reconcile plan3.md:305 with 1507 and reference the ADR from §9.5 and §9.11.
3. Re-scope T-084 (PDF/A), T-090/T-091 (Edit) and T-157 (Translate) against the answer, and give T-157 a refusal path like T-091's if shaping is refused.

## Done when
- [ ] §3.3 names a font owner, or the four dependent features are re-scoped in writing
- [ ] A stamp written by `Compose` embeds a subset font and opens correctly in Acrobat
- [ ] Bundled font licences are covered by T-005's scan or by an explicit exception record
- [ ] Unsupported scripts fail with a clear message rather than blank glyphs

description:

Separately §7.3 claims the NIF-less mode "keeps reading fully functional" while §10.3 (1897-1905) makes PDFium mandatory to create a document at all: encryption detection is a "PDFium load attempt" and `document_pages` comes from `Render.page_count` + `page_geometry`. `unavailable` means "feature disabled" (1125), which here disables document open itself. This sits under R-01, the highest-rated risk.

## Do
1. Choose one: (a) remove `Render.Client` from the behaviour and describe it as a client thumbnail-contribution path (LiveView event -> `document_pages.thumbnail_ref`), or (b) define degraded ingest where pdf.js reports page count, geometry and encryption at open and the server records them.
2. Amend T-017 and §7.3 to match, and amend §10.3 to name which steps have a client substitute.
3. State plainly what is and is not available with the NIF gone (server search, extract_text, all transforms: unavailable).

## Done when
- [ ] `Render.Client` either implements the behaviour honestly or is documented as a separate path
- [ ] Test: open a fixture with the PDFium NIF force-disabled - it either opens with client-reported metadata or fails with a message naming the remedy, and never half-opens

title: Define revision-chain semantics under undo (branch, signed, prune)
description:
## Why
F-07 (major). `{:restore_revision, id}` (plan3.md:1197-1200) is only a valid inverse at the head of a linear chain, and the plan never says what happens afterwards. Three open questions: (a) after undoing rev 5 to rev 4 and applying a new op, is the result rev 6 with `parent_revision_id = 4` (a branch, so `seq` is no longer dense and Compare's two-revision mode at 1660 must handle forks) or a rewrite (breaking append-only at 676)? (b) `digital_signatures.revision_id` (765-768) pins a signed revision - rolling `current_revision_id` past it must be forbidden and nothing says so. (c) T-172's retention job (2507) can prune a revision that a rehydrated journal (1245) still points at, turning undo into a 500.

## Do
1. Write the branch-on-undo paragraph into §7.4: pick branching (recommended - preserves append-only) and state how `seq` and `parent_revision_id` behave.
2. Add `UNIQUE (document_id, seq)` to the migration and state the invariant it encodes.
3. State the rule "never roll `current_revision_id` back past a revision that carries a signature", enforced in `Editing`.
4. Add to T-172 as an explicit precondition: refuse to prune any revision referenced by a non-undone `edit_operations.inverse` or by `digital_signatures`.

## Done when
- [ ] §7.4 defines chain topology after undo, with an example
- [ ] Migration carries `UNIQUE (document_id, seq)`
- [ ] Test: undo past a signed revision is refused with a clear message
- [ ] Test: retention leaves journal-referenced and signature-referenced revisions alone
- [ ] Compare (T-112) states how it handles two revisions on different branches

description:
## Why

phx.gen.auth wrote `config :quire, :scopes, user: [... schema_key: :user_id ...]` into config/config.exs. But §5.2 specifies `documents.owner_id` (plan3.md:676 area) and `esign_envelopes.owner_id` (:777 area).

Any later `mix phx.gen.live` or `mix phx.gen.context` run under the default scope will emit `user_id` and silently contradict the schema the plan specifies — and it will look correct, because the generator is doing exactly what it was configured to do.

## Do

2. If `owner_id`, set `schema_key: :owner_id` in the scope config, or stop using scope-aware generators for those contexts and say so.

title: doctor: assert shared_buffers, work_mem and the quire databases
description:
## Why

`mise run doctor` currently checks the PostgreSQL client version and that the server accepts connections, but asserts nothing about the configuration T-004 (pdf-0nc) is responsible for. Doctor passing is therefore not evidence that T-004 holds — which is exactly the failure mode doctor exists to prevent, and Gate 0 (pdf-4uq) grades on doctor being meaningful on a clean machine.

## Do

Add to mise-tasks/doctor, in the "System libraries" section:

1. `shared_buffers` is 512MB and `work_mem` is 16MB, read live from pg_settings — not grepped from postgresql.conf, since the two can disagree (see the deferred-restart issue).
2. `quire_dev` and `quire_test` both exist and are owned by the same role config/dev.exs and config/test.exs connect as.
3. No extension beyond `plpgsql` is installed in either database (§3.7). plpgsql ships in every PostgreSQL database by default and is not a violation.

## Done when

- doctor fails loudly if any of the three regress.
- doctor still exits 0 on this machine once the deferred restart has happened.

title: Restart PostgreSQL so shared_buffers=512MB goes live
description:
## Why

T-004 (pdf-0nc) set `shared_buffers = 512MB` and `work_mem = 16MB` in /opt/homebrew/var/postgresql@18/postgresql.conf. `work_mem` (context=user) took effect immediately, but `shared_buffers` is context=postmaster, so it needs a FULL restart, not a reload — the live value is still 128MB while the file says 512MB.

The restart was deliberately deferred: this is a single shared cluster hosting 82 databases for unrelated projects on this machine, and restarting drops every open connection to all of them.

## Do

At a moment when nothing else is using the cluster:

```
brew services restart postgresql@18
until pg_isready -q; do sleep 1; done
psql -tAc "select name, setting, unit from pg_settings where name in (\x27shared_buffers\x27,\x27work_mem\x27)"
```

Expect `shared_buffers|65536|8kB` (= 512MB) and `work_mem|16384|kB`.

## Done when

- `show shared_buffers` returns 512MB from a live connection, not just the file.

## Notes

Backup of the original config is at /opt/homebrew/var/postgresql@18/postgresql.conf.pre-quire. `fsync` was deliberately left at its default (commented, line 237) per §3.7.

title: Phase 9 — OCR
description:
OCR is a pure in-BEAM pipeline (`Quire.Ocr.Engine`, §3.3): rasterise each page with the PDFium NIF at 300 DPI → preprocess with vix (deskew, denoise, optional clean) → recognise with the Tesseract NIF → compose the output PDF by placing the recognised text as an invisible text layer over the untouched original page (sandwich mode), saved as a new revision. No intermediate files, no external orchestrator (plan3.md lines 1758-1763).

## Scope
- T-139 — `OcrWorker` running the full in-BEAM pipeline
- T-140 — OCR options UI
- T-141 — tessdata management

- T-144 — scan-and-recognise combined flow
- T-145 — auto-prompt when the document has no text layer

## Gate

description:

title: Gate 9: OCR output searchable, images unchanged, budgets hold
description:
## Acceptance gate
**Gate 9:** `scanned_300dpi.pdf` becomes searchable in Chrome's viewer; page images are visually unchanged; throughput meets §14.1; the §14.1 scheduler-stall budget holds while `:ocr` and `:render` are both saturated.

## Verify
1. OCR `scanned_300dpi.pdf` through the app, open the output in Chrome's built-in viewer, and find text via Chrome's own search.
2. Diff the rendered page images of the output against the input and confirm they are visually unchanged (the text layer is invisible and the original page is untouched).
3. Measure throughput on the target machine (Apple Silicon, plugged in, `ocr: 1`, single language, 300 DPI) and confirm ≥ 1 page/s per §14.1 line 2132.
4. Saturate the `:ocr` and `:render` queues simultaneously and confirm `:timer.tc` on an unrelated process stays under 5 ms — zero scheduler stalls per §14.1 line 2133.

title: T-127: SecurityHandler — AESV2/AESV3 encryption and permission flags
description:
## Task
`SecurityHandler`: AESV2/AESV3 encryption + permission flags per ISO 32000-2 §7.6. Password handling: never logged, assigns zeroed. Verify by opening output in Acrobat and by decrypting the encrypted fixtures.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.7 line 1677: `Quire.SecurityHandler` implements the standard security handler (AESV2 128-bit, AESV3 256-bit) per ISO 32000-2 §7.6 in pure Elixir over `:crypto` — key derivation, per-object stream/string encryption, and the `/Encrypt` dictionary. Also sets a user (open) password. Passwords MUST be posted over the LiveView channel and never logged; zero the assign immediately after use.
- plan3.md §5.4 lines 741-791 (`security_policies`).
- plan3.md Appendix C R-04, line 2665.

## Done when
- AESV2 (128-bit) and AESV3 (256-bit) encryption are implemented in pure Elixir over `:crypto`, producing a correct `/Encrypt` dictionary with key derivation and per-object stream/string encryption.
- All eight permission flags (print, print high-quality, modify, copy/extract, annotate, fill forms, extract for accessibility, assemble) are settable and are honoured when the output is opened in Acrobat.
- Passwords never appear in logs or telemetry, and the LiveView assign holding a password is zeroed immediately after use — asserted by a test.
- `encrypted_user_pw.pdf` and `encrypted_owner_pw.pdf` decrypt correctly with this handler, and output produced here opens in Acrobat with the expected restrictions.

title: T-129: Pades.Cms + Pades.Pkcs12 against RFC 5652 vectors
description:
## Task
`Pades.Cms` + `Pades.Pkcs12`: keystore parsing, CMS detached signature construction over byte ranges. Unit-test against published RFC 5652 vectors.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.7 line 1678: `Quire.Pades` (pure Elixir over OTP `:public_key`/`:crypto`): parse PKCS#12 keystores, build the CMS (PKCS#7) detached signature over the byte range … RSA and ECDSA keys.
- plan3.md §13 line 2071 (unit: PAdES + security handler against reference vectors).
- plan3.md Appendix C R-04, line 2665: RFC test vectors in unit tests.

## Done when
- `Pades.Pkcs12` parses a PKCS#12 keystore and yields the key and certificate chain for both RSA and ECDSA keys.
- `Pades.Cms` builds a detached CMS/PKCS#7 signature over a supplied byte range.
- Unit tests assert against published RFC 5652 vectors and fail if the encoding drifts — self-consistency alone is not accepted.
- Both modules are pure Elixir over OTP `:public_key`/`:crypto` with no external crypto tool or NIF.

description:

title: T-114: Signature capture — draw, type, upload; saved appearances

title: T-134: Apply redaction with mandatory post-hoc verification
description:
## Task
**Apply redaction** — PDFium object-removal path with the rasterise-and-replace fallback, plus the mandatory post-hoc text-extraction verification. Fail the job if redacted strings survive.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.7 line 1680: Two paths, in order of preference: (a) enumerate page content via PDFium and delete the text/image/vector objects intersecting the mark, then draw the overlay …; (b) rasterise the affected page at 300 DPI with the region blanked and replace the page (lossy but bulletproof — automatic fallback for pages where (a) cannot prove completeness, e.g. the mark overlaps a Type-3 glyph or an unparseable content stream). After applying, **verify** by re-extracting text and asserting the redacted strings are absent; fail the job if they are not.
- plan3.md Appendix C R-06 (line 2667) — **Critical**: fail the job rather than ship a leak.

## Done when
- Path (a) removes the intersecting text/image/vector objects via PDFium and draws the overlay, preserving the rest of the page.
- Path (b) triggers automatically wherever (a) cannot prove completeness (e.g. Type-3 glyph overlap, unparseable content stream), rasterising at 300 DPI with the region blanked and replacing the page.
- After every apply, text is re-extracted and the redacted strings are asserted absent; if any survive, the job fails and the document is not replaced.
- A test proves the redacted string is absent from text extraction and from copy of the output (Gate 8), and `redactions.applied` / `applied_revision_id` are set only on success.

title: T-124: Reset form
description:
## Task
Reset form.

title: T-109: Whiteout with the mandatory redaction warning
description:
## Task
Whiteout **with the mandatory redaction warning**.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.6 line 1659: An opaque filled rectangle matching the page background. **Must warn that this is cosmetic — the text underneath remains extractable.** Offer "Redact instead" in the same toast. This distinction is a genuine data-leak risk and the UI must be unambiguous.
- plan3.md §9.6 line 1669 (acceptance): whiteout shows the warning every time until the user dismisses it permanently.
- plan3.md §9.7 lines 1671-1688 (Create/Apply redaction — the offered alternative); §9.7 line 1688: the UI never conflates whiteout with redaction.

## Done when
- Placing a whiteout shows a warning stating the underlying text remains extractable, and the same toast offers "Redact instead" which switches to the redaction tool.
- The warning appears on every whiteout placement until the user explicitly dismisses it permanently (a persisted user setting), not merely once per session.
- A test asserts text under a whiteout is still returned by text extraction, documenting the cosmetic behaviour.
- Whiteout is never labelled or described as redaction anywhere in the UI copy.

title: T-100: Ruler with guides and Grid with snap
description:
## Task
∥ Ruler with guides. ∥ Grid with snap.

title: T-090: Floating text format bar with the full control set

Floating text format bar, full control set (§9.5).

Remove page marks (tracked marks only; explain the limitation).

title: T-099: Spell check — browser-native plus pure-Elixir document report
description:

Spell check (browser-native interactive + the pure-Elixir document report, §9.5).

## Spec

The document-wide "check document" report runs a pure-Elixir dictionary pass (compiled wordlist per language, shipped as app data) over `extract_text` output.
- plan3.md §7.3 lines 1132-1173 — `Render.extract_text`.

## Done when
- Interactive checking uses the browser's native spellcheck in `contenteditable` — no spell-check engine is shipped to the client, and no external spelling process is spawned.
- The "check document" report is produced by a pure-Elixir dictionary pass over `Render.extract_text` output, using a compiled wordlist shipped as app data.
- The language selector switches both the `contenteditable` language attribute and the wordlist used by the report.
- The report lists each misspelling with its page number and is generated without any new GPL/AGPL dependency (Appendix E line 2715).

title: T-101: Coalescing rules for typing and styling ops
description:
## Task
Coalescing rules for typing/styling ops (§7.4).

## Spec
- plan3.md §7.4 lines 1234-1236 — **Coalescing.** Consecutive `text.style` or `annot.update` ops on the same target within 800 ms MUST coalesce into one journal entry, or undo becomes useless during typing.
- plan3.md §7.4 lines 1229-1232 — undo pops the journal head; any new op clears `redo_stack`.
- plan3.md Appendix C R-08 line 2667 — coalescing is a named mitigation for undo/redo being subtly wrong across the hybrid boundary.

## Done when
- Consecutive `text.style` ops on the same target within 800 ms produce exactly one `edit_operations` row / one journal entry, asserted by a unit test that emits several ops inside the window.
- The same rule applies to `annot.update` on the same target, and ops on *different* targets or more than 800 ms apart do **not** coalesce.
- The coalesced entry's `inverse` restores the state from before the first op in the run, verified by an undo test.
- Gate 5's 50-operation edit session undoes and redoes cleanly with coalescing enabled.

title: T-112: Compare — text diff plus visual pixel diff, side-by-side
description:
## Task

description:

title: T-091: Edit mode — rewrite existing text runs, refuse gracefully
description:
## Task
Edit mode: identify existing runs via PDFium spans; rewrite content streams via `Compose`; refuse gracefully on non-embedded/subset fonts with an OCR suggestion.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.5 lines 1591-1596 — **Edit mode** (best-effort): use PDFium's text extraction with per-character bboxes and font metrics to identify a run, then rewrite that run's content stream via `Quire.Compose`. Refuse gracefully (with a clear message) when the font is not embedded or is subset without the needed glyphs, offering "convert to editable text via OCR" instead.
- plan3.md §3.3 line 306 — `Quire.Compose` is pure-Elixir content-stream generation.
- plan3.md Appendix C R-05 line 2664 — two explicit modes; refuse clearly rather than corrupting; set expectations in-product.

## Done when
- A run is identified from PDFium per-character bboxes and font metrics, and the rewritten content stream is produced by `Compose`, verified by a test that edits text in `simple_text.pdf` and re-extracts it.
- Editing text whose font is not embedded, or is subset without the needed glyphs, **refuses** with a clear message and offers "convert to editable text via OCR" — asserted by a test on such a fixture; the document is left byte-unchanged in that case.
- The UI states that Edit mode is best-effort before the user commits (R-05).
- Every successful edit emits a `text.edit` op whose inverse is captured in the same statement via PG18 `RETURNING OLD.*, NEW.*` (§7.4 lines 1202-1208).

title: T-102: AnnotEditHook driving pdf.js editor layer via PDFViewer
description:
## Task
`AnnotEditHook` driving pdf.js's editor layer **through `PDFViewer.annotationEditorMode` + `annotationEditorParams` and the EventBus** — do not instantiate `AnnotationEditorLayer` yourself (§9.6).

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.6 lines 1639-1669; the entry-point warning is line 1652: `AnnotationEditorLayer` is exported from `build/pdf.mjs`, **not** from `web/pdf_viewer.mjs`, and cannot be driven standalone (it needs an `AnnotationEditorUIManager`).
- plan3.md §7.4 lines 1174-1246 (journal integration for client-side ops)
- plan3.md §14.3 lines 2146-2165 (store annotations in PDF points; use `PageViewport.convertToPdfPoint`)

## Done when
- `assets/js/hooks/annot_edit_hook.js` (or equivalent) contains no `new AnnotationEditorLayer(...)` and no import of `AnnotationEditorLayer` — mode changes go through `PDFViewer.annotationEditorMode` and parameter changes through `annotationEditorParams`.
- Editor state changes are observed via EventBus events (e.g. `annotationeditormodechanged`, `annotationeditorstateschanged`), not by polling the layer.
- A LiveView test drives an annotation-mode switch end to end and asserts the resulting op reaches the journal.
- Coordinates crossing the hook boundary are PDF points produced by the shared geometry module, not inline maths.

description:
## Task
`DocMutateHook` over `@cantoo/pdf-lib` 2.7.4.

## Spec

- plan3.md §4 line 558 and §6 line 982 — `DocMutateHook` → `@cantoo/pdf-lib`; `mutate.js` is a thin facade over it.

## Done when

- The hook applies a mutation optimistically and pushes the op to the LiveView, and a rejected op triggers a `revert` event that restores the prior bytes (§7.4 line 1217).
- `Save` uploads the hook's current bytes as a new revision (§7.4 lines 1238-1241), covered by a Playwright test.

Insert image (with server-side format normalisation to PNG/JPEG via vix).

title: Gate 6: annotations round-trip losslessly; ink smooth at 120 Hz
description:
## Acceptance gate
**Gate 6:** all annotation types round-trip losslessly; ink is smooth at
120 Hz; the whiteout warning is unmissable.

## Verify
1. Every annotation type implemented in this phase (text markup, sticky note, ink, all nine shapes, stamps, file attachment, free-text callout, measure, whiteout) is authored here, opened in Acrobat, and re-opened here with no loss of kind, geometry, colour, opacity, author, contents or replies (T-113).
2. Ink capture stays smooth at a 120 Hz pointer rate: coalesced pointer events are all consumed and stroke-to-visible latency is under the §14.1 16 ms budget with no per-sample server round-trip.
3. The whiteout warning appears on every placement until permanently dismissed, states that the underlying text remains extractable, and offers "Redact instead" — and no UI copy conflates whiteout with redaction.

title: T-093: Link tool and Add Action modal, JS actions off by default
description:
## Task
Link tool + **Add Action** modal, all action types; JS actions **off by default**.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.5 line 1602 — **Link**: drag a rectangle → opens the **Add Action** modal; also converts selected text into a link.
- plan3.md §9.5 lines 1623-1633 — the modal is a card grid of action types with an overflow `⋮`, then a type-specific form, then `Apply` (disabled until valid) / `Cancel`. Types: Open web page (URL with scheme validation, "open in new window"), Open file (a `Ref` picker), Go to page (page number + zoom/fit, a named destination); overflow: Go to named destination, Execute menu item, Submit form, Reset form, Show/hide field, **Run JavaScript** (⚠️ default **off**; if enabled, never execute it server-side and sandbox it in the viewer via pdf.js's `PDFScriptingManager` + `pdf.sandbox.mjs`).
- plan3.md §7.4 line 1190 — `link.add`, `link.edit` op kinds.

## Done when
- All nine action types are implemented, with the first three in the card grid and the rest behind the `⋮` overflow, enumerated by a LiveView test.
- `Apply` is disabled until the type-specific form is valid, and URL fields reject schemes outside the allowlist.
- **Run JavaScript is off by default**: a test asserts the default setting is disabled, that no JS action is ever evaluated server-side, and that when enabled it runs only through `PDFScriptingManager` + `pdf.sandbox.mjs` in the viewer.
- Dragging a rectangle and converting selected text both create a link, each emitting a `link.add` op.

title: Gate 5: 50-op session undo/redo clean; identical in 3 renderers
description:
## Acceptance gate
**Gate 5:** a 50-operation edit session undoes and redoes cleanly; output renders identically in Acrobat, Chrome and Preview.

## Verify
1. A scripted edit session of at least 50 operations (mixing add-text, style, image insert, link, and stamping ops) can be undone step by step back to the original document state, with the final state byte-equivalent to the starting revision.
2. The same session can then be redone step by step back to the fully edited state, with no operation lost or reordered.
3. The saved output opens and renders identically in Adobe Acrobat, Chrome (pdf.js) and macOS Preview — compared by rendering each at 150 DPI and pixel-diffing (§13 line 2077).

title: Fix the doctor/bootstrap defects that block Gate 0 on a clean machine
description:
## Why
F-16, F-18, F-19 (minor, but Gate 0 cannot pass as written). Three defects in the reproducibility contract that §0 rule 3 (plan3.md:50-54) makes load-bearing. (a) `ulimit -n 8192` is set only in the `server` task (2616) yet asserted unconditionally (2654); `ulimit` is a shell builtin so mise's `[env]` cannot set it globally, and `doctor`/`check` see macOS's 256 - so Gate 0's "doctor is green on a clean checkout" (2215-2216) fails on day one. (b) §3.6.6 says "Homebrew-installed binaries are already clear" of quarantine (476-478); true for formulae, false for casks - and the Brewfile's one cask is `chromium` (2635), the exact binary whose misleading "killed: 9" the section describes. (c) Appendix D allows OTP 27 (2688) against §3.1's emphatic `-otp-28` pin (210), and B.3 (2646-2654) has no `:crypto`/OpenSSL row despite `--enable-dynamic-ssl-lib` (428-437) being the weakest seam (418-425) and R-14 assuming the check exists.

## Do
1. Set the ulimit at the `[tasks]` level, and split `doctor:fast` (versions, config, ulimit) from `doctor:full` (NIF + OCR + Chromium round trips). Point the pre-push hook at `doctor:fast`.
2. Correct plan3.md:476-478 to "formulae are clear, casks are quarantined by default"; add `args: { "no-quarantine": true }` (or an `xattr -dr` step) to bootstrap step 4 and assert it beside the Chromium `--version` probe.
3. Delete "27 acceptable" from Appendix D; add a B.3 row asserting `:crypto.info_lib/0` against the Homebrew `openssl@3` version, with "reinstall OTP" as the remedy.

## Done when
- [ ] `mise run doctor` reports >= 8192 descriptors from any task
- [ ] A freshly bootstrapped machine runs a chromic_pdf conversion with no manual xattr step
- [ ] doctor fails loudly when OpenSSL drifts from the OTP build
- [ ] Gate 0 passes on a fresh macOS user account with no manual intervention

title: §13 testing strategy has no auth layer despite conn_case.ex being rewritten
description:
## Why

phx.gen.auth injected into test/support/conn_case.ex and config/test.exs during T-200, and added register_and_log_in_user / set_password style helpers via test/support/fixtures/accounts_fixtures.ex. plan3.md §13 describes the testing strategy and does not mention authentication at all — so every future LiveView test written from §13 will 401 or crash on a missing current_scope, and the author will not know why.

## Do

Add a short subsection to §13 covering: which helper logs a test session in, that `@current_scope` must be passed to `<Layouts.app>`, and that an unauthenticated LiveView mount is expected to redirect rather than render.

## Done when

- §13 tells someone writing their first LiveView test how to get an authenticated session.

title: T-181: Wire title-bar window controls to the shell
description:
## Task
Window controls in the title bar wired to the shell.

## Spec

- plan3.md §12.1 step 3, lines 1990-1992 — window creation; `on_exit` → `System.stop()`

title: T-178: Switch to Storage.Local and wire pick_open/pick_save to the dialog plugin
description:
## Task
Switch to `Storage.Local`; wire `pick_open`/`pick_save` to the Tauri dialog plugin via a hook.

## Spec
- plan3.md §12.1 step 7, lines 2007-2008 — "`Storage.Local` becomes the adapter; `pick_open`/`pick_save` call the `dialog` plugin via a colocated hook and return real paths."
- plan3.md §7.1, lines 1010-1017, 1054-1057 — dispatch is by **runtime lookup** (`Application.fetch_env!(:quire, :storage_adapter)`), never compile-time; `Storage.Local` is plain `File.*`; `pick_open`/`pick_save` push a request to the client which returns a real path over a LiveView event
- plan3.md §7.1, lines 1058-1063 — the File System Access API is deliberately not used

## Done when
- Switching to the desktop build is a config change to `:storage_adapter` only — no `defdelegate` and no compile-time adapter reference exists in `Quire.Storage`.

- The shared `StorageCase` suite passes against `Storage.Local` as well as `Storage.Web`.
- `grep -r showOpenFilePicker assets/` returns nothing.

title: Gate 12: licence gating holds server-side; one cloud round-trip works
description:
## Acceptance gate
**Gate 12:** a Standard-tier user cannot invoke a Premium-tier worker even by hand-crafting a LiveView event; cloud round-trip works for at least one provider.

(plan3.md lines 2509-2511)

## Verify
1. Signed in as a Standard-tier user, push a hand-crafted LiveView event naming a Premium-only feature (e.g. OCR): the event handler refuses it and no Oban job is enqueued.
2. Bypass the event handler and enqueue the Premium-only Oban job directly for that Standard-tier user: the worker itself refuses and the job fails with a licensing error — proving the gate exists in the worker, not just the UI and handler (§11.2 lines 1942-1945).
3. Connect at least one cloud provider from backstage → Add account, browse it, open a remote file into the workspace, and save back to that provider: the round-trip completes and the file content matches.
4. The connector's stored tokens are encrypted at rest in `cloud_connections` (§5.6 line 828).

title: T-194: README (tested on a fresh account), ARCHITECTURE.md, ADR log, runbook
description:

Documentation: README (with the §3.6 bootstrap), ARCHITECTURE.md, ADR log, runbook. The README's setup section is tested by doing it on a fresh macOS user account — if it takes more than the bootstrap sequence in §3.6.1, fix the setup, not the README.

title: T-196: Reproducibility check — fresh clone, bootstrap, doctor, check, e2e
description:
## Task
∥ Reproducibility check: clone into a fresh directory on a second machine (or a new macOS user account), run the §3.6.1 bootstrap, `mise run doctor`, `mise run check`, `mise run e2e`. Everything green with no manual intervention. Without a container image, this is the only real evidence that the `mise.toml` + `Brewfile` contract holds.

## Spec
- plan3.md §3.6.1 Bootstrap order, lines 392-409 — the seven steps; "`mise run doctor` ... must exit non-zero on any missing or wrong-versioned component"
- plan3.md §3.6.2 What mise owns, lines 410-426
- plan3.md Appendix B, lines 2601-2655 — `mise.toml`, `Brewfile`, B.3 what T-013 must assert
- plan3.md §13, line 2095 — "T-196 covers the rest."

## Done when
- A fresh clone on a second machine or new macOS user account completes the §3.6.1 sequence with **zero** manual steps beyond those seven.
- `mise run doctor`, `mise run check` and `mise run e2e` all exit 0 on that fresh environment.
- Any component the run revealed as assumed-present is added to the `Brewfile` or `mise.toml` and to `mise run doctor`'s assertion table (Appendix E, line 2720).
- Machine-specific values needed by the run live in the gitignored `.mise.local.toml`, and the fresh run works without one where possible.

title: T-191: Telemetry dashboards on LiveDashboard — no metrics stack
description:
## Task
Telemetry dashboards: engine durations, queue depth, render latency, error rates. LiveDashboard is enough locally; do not stand up a metrics stack for one machine.

- Saturating the `:render` and `:ocr` queues moves the queue-depth and latency metrics visibly — checked during the T-189 load run.
- No Prometheus/Grafana/StatsD service is added to the `Brewfile`, `mise.toml` or dependency list.
- Access to the dashboard route is authenticated, not open.

title: T-168: Cloud file browser in the backstage Computer pane

Do not attempt to emulate drives."; "**one component, two adapters, no branching in the LiveView.**"

title: T-182: macOS entitlements, codesign step and notarisation
description:
## Task
macOS: entitlements (`allow-jit`, `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`, `allow-dyld-environment-variables`, `disable-library-validation`), codesign step, notarisation.

## Spec

title: T-174: ElixirKit wiring — PubSub, release spawn, ready:<url>, on_exit stop
description:
## Task
ElixirKit wiring: PubSub listen, spawn release, `ready:<url>`, window creation, `on_exit` → `System.stop()`.

## Spec
- plan3.md §12.1 steps 2-3, lines 1988-1992 — "Rust: ElixirKit PubSub listen on a loopback TCP port, spawn the release with `ELIXIRKIT_PUBSUB` in its env." and "The Elixir supervision tree adds the ElixirKit PubSub child with an `on_exit` that stops the VM, and broadcasts `ready:<url>` once the endpoint is listening. Rust opens the window at that URL."
- plan3.md §12.1 preamble, lines 1979-1983 — ElixirKit 0.1.0, no `elixirkit` crate on crates.io; the Rust side is a path dependency into the Hex package
- Appendix D, line 2705 (ElixirKit 0.1.0 — Phase 13 only)

## Done when
- The Rust side listens on a loopback TCP port and spawns the release with `ELIXIRKIT_PUBSUB` set; `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` references elixirkit as a **path** dependency into the Hex package, not crates.io.
- The supervision tree includes the ElixirKit PubSub child and broadcasts `ready:<url>` only after the endpoint is listening; Rust opens the window at exactly that URL.
- Closing the window fires `on_exit` → `System.stop()` and the BEAM process exits — verified by checking no orphaned `beam.smp` remains after quit.
- Killing the release out from under the shell surfaces a plain-language error rather than a blank window (Appendix E, line 2719).

title: T-189: Load test on this machine; tune and record the §7.5 queue numbers
description:
## Task
Load test on *this* machine: 20 concurrent conversions, 50 concurrent viewers. Tune the §7.5 queue numbers against real measurements and record them. Assert the §14.1 scheduler-stall budget while `:ocr` and `:render` are both saturated.

## Spec
- plan3.md §7.5 Oban queues, lines 1247-1297 — the concurrency table and the two warnings: "`convert: 1` is about Chromium, not conservatism" and "`ocr: 1` and `render: 4` interact ... treat the numbers above as a starting point and tune them there"
- plan3.md §14.1 Budgets, lines 2115-2133 — especially "**Scheduler stall during OCR + render** | **0** — `:timer.tc` on an unrelated process stays under 5 ms while both queues are saturated" and "**BEAM RSS, idle, 3 documents open** | **< 500 MB**"
- plan3.md §13, line 2079 — Load | `Benchee` | 20 concurrent conversions; assert no queue starvation and no scheduler stall

## Done when
- A Benchee load test drives 20 concurrent conversions and 50 concurrent viewers on the target machine, plugged in (§14.1 line 2117), and no queue starves.
- With `:ocr` and `:render` both saturated, `:timer.tc` on an unrelated process stays under 5 ms for the whole run — the assertion is in the test, not a manual observation.
- The tuned `render`/`transform`/`convert`/`ocr` concurrencies are **recorded** in the repo alongside the measurements that justify them, and the §7.5 table is updated to match.
- `convert` concurrency is not raised above 1 without an explicit browser-instance pool with a hard cap (§7.5 lines 1270-1274).
- Measurements taken on battery are excluded and noted as such (§14.1 lines 2117-2120).

title: T-184: Linux deb + AppImage; test ribbon and pdf.js on webkit2gtk
description:
## Task
∥ Linux: deb + AppImage. **Test the ribbon and pdf.js on webkit2gtk** — this is where CSS breaks.

## Spec
- plan3.md §12.4 Platform webview caveat, lines 2055-2063 — "**webkit2gtk** on Linux. Test the ribbon and the pdf.js canvas on all three before shipping; Linux is where CSS surprises appear."
- plan3.md §12.3, lines 2051-2053 — "**Electron** — pick this only if webkit2gtk on older Linux distros breaks the UI."
- plan3.md §7.1, lines 1058-1063 — FSA API is unsupported in webkit2gtk, which is why it is forbidden

## Done when
- `.deb` and AppImage artefacts build and both install/run on a target Linux distro.
- The full ribbon (§8.2) is visually checked on webkit2gtk at the three §13 widths and no control is clipped, misaligned or invisible; findings are fixed in CSS, not worked around per-platform.
- The pdf.js canvas renders a corpus PDF correctly under webkit2gtk, including scroll and zoom.
- Opening a file from a real folder works on Linux (Gate 13).
- If webkit2gtk breaks the UI irrecoverably, the §12.3 Electron escape hatch is invoked deliberately and recorded — not adopted silently.

title: T-177: Localhost auth plug — per-run token, secure_compare, ETS sessions
description:
## Task
Localhost auth plug (32-byte per-run token, `secure_compare`, ETS sessions). Keep `check_origin: true`.

## Spec
- plan3.md §12.2 Security for the localhost server, lines 2018-2035 — "Anything running on the machine can reach `127.0.0.1:PORT`. Mint 32 random bytes per app run, hand them to the webview as a query token on first navigation, compare with `Plug.Crypto.secure_compare/2`, promote to a session flag, and 401 everything else. Use an **ETS session store** rather than cookies inside the embedded webview." and "**Keep `check_origin: true`.** ... Do not set it to `false` — Phoenix raises at boot if both `check_origin` and `check_csrf` are false, and disabling origin checking opens CSWSH."

## Spec (cont.)
- plan3.md §12.1 step 5, lines 1996-2002

## Done when
- A 32-byte token is minted per app run, passed as a query token on first navigation, and compared with `Plug.Crypto.secure_compare/2` — a test asserts a wrong token yields 401 and that comparison is not `==`.
- Sessions live in an ETS session store, not cookies; a request without the promoted session flag gets 401 on every route.
- `check_origin: true` remains set for the desktop endpoint; `grep check_origin` shows no `false`.
- Two app runs produce different tokens, so a token captured from run 1 is rejected in run 2.
- Telemetry or a log line records rejected requests (Appendix E, line 2718).

title: T-192: Error taxonomy — every failure maps to a message and a docs link
description:
## Task
Error taxonomy: every failure maps to a user-facing message + a docs link.

## Spec
- plan3.md §8.6 Progress, errors, empty states, lines 1436-1446 — "Failures: a toast with a plain-language message and a 'Details' disclosure showing the engine's structured error. **Never surface raw engine output as the primary message.**"
- plan3.md §7.2, lines 1096-1100 — a stuck NIF call is abandoned by the job and surfaced as a structured error
- plan3.md §10.3, lines 1910-1914 — corrupt-file handling: "Files that even tolerant loading rejects get a clear, specific error — never a crash."

## Done when
- A single error-taxonomy module maps every error term the app can produce to a plain-language message plus a docs link; a test enumerates the taxonomy and fails on an unmapped term.
- Error toasts show the mapped message as the primary text with the structured engine error behind a "Details" disclosure — never the reverse (§8.6 lines 1440-1442).
- `corrupt_xref.pdf` and an unopenable file from the §13 corpus each produce a specific mapped error, not a crash or a stack trace.
- Every docs link in the taxonomy resolves to an existing section of the T-194 documentation.

title: T-190: Security review — deps, SSRF, uploads, traversal, CSP, secret sweep
description:
## Task
Security review: dependency audit, SSRF, upload validation (magic bytes, not extensions), path traversal, rate limits, CSP. Also: Sobelow clean, `.mise.local.toml` in `.gitignore`, and a history sweep for any secret that ever got committed.

## Spec
- plan3.md §3.4 Native-Elixir contract, lines 344-376 and §3.5 lines 377-383 — dependency-licence scan fails the build on any AGPL/GPL entry
- plan3.md §12.2 Security for the localhost server, lines 2018-2035
- plan3.md §7.2, lines 1093-1095 — bounded inputs: "a 4 GB malformed PDF must be rejected by policy, not by a NIF crash"
- plan3.md §7.5 line 1280 references this task's load test as T-190; §15 line 2546 assigns the load test to T-189 — follow §15

## Done when
- `mix deps.audit` (or equivalent) and the licence scan run in `mise run check` and both exit 0; no GPL/AGPL entry (§3.5 line 383).
- Uploads are validated by **magic bytes**, not file extension — a test renames a `.txt` to `.pdf` and asserts rejection.
- URL-fetch paths reject private/link-local/loopback targets (SSRF), asserted by tests; oversized inputs are rejected by policy before reaching any NIF.
- Path traversal is impossible: no caller-supplied string reaches the filesystem outside `Storage` (Appendix E, line 2714).
- `mix sobelow --exit` is clean, a CSP is set on the endpoint, and rate limits exist on the public signer route and auth endpoints.
- `.mise.local.toml` is in `.gitignore`, and a git-history secret sweep (e.g. gitleaks over all refs) reports nothing (Appendix E, line 2723).

title: T-180: Native-library redistribution and otool -L audit (budget > 1 day)
description:
## Task
Native-library redistribution: verify the PDFium and libvips dylibs travel inside their NIF artefacts; make Tesseract + tessdata redistributable per the T-019 ADR (static link preferred); `otool -L` every binary and confirm nothing links back into `/opt/homebrew`. **Budget more than a day for this task alone.**

## Spec
- plan3.md §12.1 step 8, lines 2009-2016 — "the PDFium dylib travels inside the `ex_pdfium` artefact and libvips inside the vix artefact. Tesseract + tessdata must become **redistributable artefacts you ship**, not a Homebrew formula you assume — either statically linked into the NIF build (preferred; decide in T-019's ADR) or bundled dylibs with `install_name_tool` fix-ups. Verify with `otool -L` that no bundled binary links back into `/opt/homebrew`. **`File.chmod!(path, 0o755)` on first use** for anything executable — do not assume the executable bit survives archive round-trips."
- plan3.md §3.5 Licensing rules, lines 379-383 — libvips is LGPL-2.1: **dynamic linking only, do not statically link**

## Done when
- A script runs `otool -L` over every binary in the built bundle and fails if any path contains `/opt/homebrew`; it is wired into the packaging step.
- PDFium ships inside the `ex_pdfium` artefact and libvips inside the vix artefact, **dynamically linked** (§3.5 line 382).
- Tesseract + tessdata ship as redistributable artefacts following T-019's ADR — static link if that is what the ADR chose, otherwise bundled dylibs with `install_name_tool` fix-ups.
- Anything executable gets `File.chmod!(path, 0o755)` on first use.
- The app launches on a machine with Homebrew's Tesseract and libvips uninstalled.

title: T-176: Tauri remote.urls capability for http://localhost:* plus dialog/fs perms
description:
## Task
`remote.urls` capability for **`http://localhost:*`** (not `127.0.0.1` — §12.1 step 5); dialog + fs permissions.

## Spec
- plan3.md §12.1 step 6, lines 2003-2006 — "Set `remote: {\"urls\": [\"http://localhost:*\"]}` in the Tauri capability, or none of the `dialog`/`fs` permissions apply to your localhost-served page. This is the single most common Tauri-v2 mistake with this architecture."
- plan3.md §12.1 step 5, lines 1996-2002 — `check_origin: true` compares the Origin **host**; `127.0.0.1` does not equal `localhost`, so navigating to `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` produces a 403 on the LiveView socket

## Done when
- The Tauri capability file contains `remote: {"urls": ["http://localhost:*"]}` and no `127.0.0.1` entry.
- The `dialog` and `fs` permissions are listed in that same capability and actually resolve from the localhost-served page — proven by a successful `pick_open` call from the running app.
- The webview navigates to `http://localhost:PORT`; a manual test navigating to `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` reproduces the documented 403 on the LiveView socket, confirming why the localhost form is required.

title: T-179: Real Local Folders and drive listing — adapter only, no LiveView changes
description:
## Task
Real Local Folders + drive listing in the backstage Computer pane — **no LiveView changes**, adapter only. Verify this.

This is the payoff for the §7.1 abstraction: **one component, two adapters, no branching in the LiveView.**"

## Done when

- `git diff` for this task touches no file under `lib/quire_web/live/` and no context module — only the `Storage.Local` adapter and config. This is stated in the task as something to **verify**, and it is the phase gate's third clause.
- The same Computer-pane component renders both web and desktop variants with no build-type branching.
- Selecting a drive or folder lists its contents without any path leaking out of the adapter (Appendix E, line 2714).

title: T-172: Retention job pruning old revisions and scratch storage
description:
## Task
Retention job: prune old revisions and scratch storage.

## Spec
- plan3.md §7.5 Oban queues, lines 1256-1268 — the `maintenance` queue, concurrency 1, "Retention"; Oban Pruner (7 days), Lifeline (30 min rescue), Reindexer

title: T-187: Dark mode completion

title: Phase 13 — Desktop packaging
description:
Wrap the existing web app in a Tauri v2 shell driving an Elixir release as a child process over ElixirKit. "**Do not write any desktop-specific code before Phase 13.** If §7.1 and §7.2 were followed, this phase is additive." (§12, lines 1966-1967). What remains is genuinely desktop work: the shell, native file dialogs, localhost auth, native-library redistribution, code signing and notarisation, and the two platforms you have not been developing on (lines 1969-1975).

## Scope
- T-173 `src-tauri/`, Tauri 2.11.x, `beforeBuildCommand`, `bundle.resources`
- T-174 ElixirKit wiring and window creation
- T-175 Port + `SECRET_KEY_BASE` injection from Rust
- T-176 `remote.urls` capability for `http://localhost:*`; dialog + fs permissions
- T-177 Localhost auth plug (32-byte token, ETS sessions, `check_origin: true`)
- T-178 Switch to `Storage.Local`; wire `pick_open`/`pick_save`
- T-179 Real Local Folders + drive listing — adapter only
- T-180 Native-library redistribution and `otool -L` audit
- T-181 Window controls in the title bar
- T-182 macOS entitlements, codesign, notarisation
- T-183 ∥ Windows MSI/NSIS, signing, WebView2
- T-184 ∥ Linux deb + AppImage; test on webkit2gtk
- T-185 Auto-update

## Gate
**Gate 13:** the app builds and runs on all three platforms; opening a file from a real folder works; **no LiveView or context code changed in this phase** (if it did, §7.1 was violated — fix that instead).

## Spec
- §7.1 Storage — lines 998-1070
- §7.2 Engine — lines 1071-1131
- §12 Desktop packaging — lines 1964-2064 (§12.1 1977-2016, §12.2 2018-2035, §12.3 2037-2053, §12.4 2055-2063)
- §10.2 Computer pane, desktop build — lines 1874-1887
- Appendix D versions — lines 2704-2705

title: T-169: Recent documents — pin, remove, clear all, sort, thumbnails

Recent documents: pin, remove, clear all, sort, thumbnails.

title: T-173: Add src-tauri with Tauri 2.11.x, release build step and bundle.resources
description:

Add `src-tauri/`, Tauri 2.11.x, `beforeBuildCommand` release step, `bundle.resources`. Rust comes from mise, already present since Phase 0 — do not add rustup separately, and do not let Tauri's installer script add a second toolchain.

title: T-195: Visual regression across all tabs, both themes, three widths
description:
## Task
Visual regression across all tabs, both themes, three widths. Three *platforms* only once Phase 13 exists; until then `darwin-arm64` baselines are the whole suite (§13).

title: T-186: Full a11y audit, keyboard-only walkthrough, screen-reader pass

Full a11y audit; keyboard-only walkthrough of every feature; screen-reader pass.

- Every `Ctrl/⌘` shortcut in the §8.5 table (lines 1424-1434) is verified live, including `Alt` ribbon access keys and `Esc` cancelling the active tool.

title: Gate 14: ship
description:
## Acceptance gate
**Gate 14:** ship.

(plan3.md line 2556)

## Verify
1. T-186's axe-core run reports zero critical a11y violations and the keyboard-only walkthrough covers every feature.

title: Gate 10: 3-signer sequential envelope completes through a tunnel
description:
## Acceptance gate
**Gate 10:** a 3-signer sequential envelope completes end-to-end **through a tunnel** (§1.2); the audit certificate matches the recorded events; tampering with the completed document fails validation.

## Verify
1. Stand up a tunnel (`cloudflared`, `ngrok` or equivalent) pointed at the local endpoint with `PHX_HOST` set to the tunnel hostname, and confirm §12.2 origin checking was not weakened to make it work (§1.2 lines 168-174).
2. Create an envelope with 3 signers in sequential order and drive it to completion, each signer reaching `/sign/:token` over the tunnel, confirming signer N+1 cannot sign before signer N.
3. Open the generated certificate of completion and confirm every entry matches the `esign_audit_events` rows for that envelope — created, sent, viewed (IP + user agent + timestamp), each field completed, signed, completed, downloaded.
4. Modify a byte of the completed document and confirm signature validation fails, both in this app's Signatures panel and in Acrobat.

- Signing is refused until every required field assigned to that signer is completed.
- Tokens are single-purpose (unusable after completion), expire, and are rate-limited — each property has its own test.
- The route works end-to-end through a tunnel with `PHX_HOST` set to the tunnel hostname, and `check_origin`/§12.2 origin checking is **not** weakened to achieve it.
- The page is keyboard accessible with `aria-label` on icon-only controls, has light and dark variants, and implements loading, empty and error states.

title: T-167: Cloud connectors with cloak_ecto-encrypted tokens
description:
## Task
Cloud connectors: Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box OAuth; S3/WebDAV manual. Tokens encrypted with `cloak_ecto`. (The S3 *connector* is somewhere the user's files come from — do not wire it into the `Storage` *backend*; those are different seams.)

## Spec
- plan3.md §5.6 Cloud connections, lines 819-828 — the `cloud_connections` schema; "Tokens MUST be encrypted at rest (`cloak_ecto` or equivalent)."
- plan3.md §10.2 Backstage → Add account, lines 1888-1891
- plan3.md §7.1 Storage, lines 1036-1053 — the `:s3` *backend* is a stub that raises; do not confuse it with this connector

## Done when
- OAuth flows complete for Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and Box, and S3/WebDAV accept manual credentials, each producing a `cloud_connections` row.
- `access_token_encrypted`/`refresh_token_encrypted` are unreadable in the raw table — a test reads the column directly and asserts it is not the plaintext token.
- `Quire.Storage`'s `:s3` backend module is still the raising stub from §7.1: no connector code references `:storage_backend` or `Storage.Web`'s backend config.
- Browsing a connected account streams the chosen file into `Storage`, returning a `Ref` — no path escapes the adapter (Appendix E, line 2714).
- Cloud round-trip (upload then re-open) works for at least one provider (Gate 12, lines 2509-2511).

title: T-164: Licensing tiers, allows?/2 and <.gated> enforced in three places
description:
## Task
Licensing tiers + `allows?/2` + `<.gated>` component; enforce in component, event handler **and** worker.

## Spec
- plan3.md §11.2 Licensing, lines 1930-1949 — the Trial/Standard/Premium/Business table, `Quire.Licensing.allows?(user, :feature_key)`, `<.gated feature={:ocr}>`, "Gate in **three** places or it leaks: the component, the LiveView event handler, and the Oban worker. Never rely on hiding UI alone."
- plan3.md §7.5 Oban queues, lines 1247-1297 (the workers that must check)

## Done when
- `Quire.Licensing.allows?/2` returns the §11.2 table's tier→feature mapping, with a unit test per tier.
- `<.gated feature={...}>` renders an upsell overlay instead of the control when `allows?/2` is false.
- A LiveView test that pushes a Premium-only event as a Standard-tier user gets a refusal, not the action.
- An Oban worker test enqueuing a Premium-only job for a Standard-tier user fails the job with a licensing error — the check exists in the worker itself, not only in the caller (Gate 12, lines 2509-2511).
- User-facing refusal text is plain language, not engine or exception output (Appendix E, line 2719).

title: T-146: Envelope data model + state machine with guarded transitions
description:
## Task
Envelope data model + state machine with guarded transitions.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.9 lines 1717-1753 (`esign_envelopes` + `esign_signers` + `esign_fields`, required states)
- plan3.md §5.4 lines 741-792 (forms, security, signing schemas)

## Done when
- Migrations create `esign_envelopes`, `esign_signers` and `esign_fields` with the fields named in §9.9 line 1727 (signer name, email, order, role; field type per signer).
- The envelope state machine covers created → sent → viewed → signed/declined → completed/voided/expired, and illegal transitions are rejected in the context function, not merely hidden in the UI.

title: T-151: Audit event capture + certificate-of-completion PDF
description:
## Task
Audit event capture (all events in §9.9) + certificate-of-completion PDF (PDFium page objects).

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.9 lines 1738-1743 ("**Audit trail** (`esign_audit_events`) MUST record: envelope created, sent, viewed (with IP + user agent + timestamp), each field completed, signed, declined, completed, downloaded. Generate a **certificate of completion** PDF (built with PDFium page objects) appended to the final document")

## Done when
- `esign_audit_events` records every event listed in §9.9 line 1738: created, sent, viewed (with IP, user agent and timestamp), each field completed, signed, declined, completed, downloaded — each with a test that the event is written.
- The certificate of completion is generated with PDFium page objects (not an HTML/Chromium render) and appended to the final document.
- The certificate's contents match the recorded `esign_audit_events` rows for the envelope, asserted in a test that compares the two.

title: T-156: Translation.Provider behaviour + real impl + default Provider.Null
description:
## Task
`Translation.Provider` behaviour + one real implementation + `Provider.Null` (the default — returns source text with a "translation disabled" banner, so a fresh clone runs and the suite costs nothing).

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.11 lines 1794-1803 ("Provider behind a `Quire.Translation.Provider` behaviour so the LLM/MT vendor is swappable... Ship a `Provider.Null` implementation that returns the source text unchanged with a visible 'translation disabled' banner, and make it the **default**")
- plan3.md §9.11 lines 1799-1800 (the API key lives in `.mise.local.toml` (gitignored), never in `config/*.exs` and never in the repo)

## Done when
- `Quire.Translation.Provider` is a behaviour with at least one real implementation and `Provider.Null`, and swapping providers requires no change outside config.
- `Provider.Null` is the configured default: a fresh clone runs the whole test suite with zero network calls and zero billing, and returns source text with a visible "translation disabled" banner.
- The real provider's API key is read from `.mise.local.toml` (gitignored) — grep of `config/*.exs` and the repo history shows no key committed.
- Dialyzer is clean on the behaviour callbacks and both implementations.

title: Phase 11 — Translate
description:
Document translation behind a swappable `Quire.Translation.Provider` behaviour: extract text with layout (PDFium spans) → translate → re-render with `Quire.Compose`, in overlay, sidecar or replace mode. "Reflow is the hard part" — translated text is routinely 20–40 % longer than the source (lines 1812-1815). Translation is the only v1 feature that sends **document content** to a third party, so it ships defaulting to `Provider.Null` with explicit consent and disclosure in Settings (lines 1799-1810).

## Scope
- T-156 — `Translation.Provider` behaviour + one real impl + `Provider.Null`
- T-157 — translate document in all three modes
- T-158 — shrink-to-fit + overflow reflow with a review list
- T-159 — selection translate popup, translate comments, glossary
- T-160 — cost estimation + `translation_cache`
- T-161 — consent and provider disclosure in Settings

## Gate
**Gate 11:** translation of a 20-page document preserves layout acceptably and flags every overflowed region in the review list; with `Provider.Null` configured the tab renders, explains itself and makes no network call; the cache prevents a re-translation of unchanged text.

## Spec
- §9.11 Translate — lines 1781-1816
- §11.3 Settings (Privacy & translation) — lines 1950-1963
- §5.5 Jobs, OCR, translation (`translation_cache`) — lines 793-818
- §14.3 The coordinate system — lines 2146-2168

title: T-157: Translate document in overlay, sidecar and replace modes
description:
## Task
Translate document in all three modes (overlay, sidecar, replace) via `Compose`.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.11 lines 1787-1789 (**Translate document**: extract text with layout (PDFium spans) → translate → re-render with `Quire.Compose`; **Overlay** (translated text over the original, original preserved underneath), **Sidecar** (side-by-side bilingual output), **Replace** (translated text replaces the original in place — best effort, reflow issues expected))
- plan3.md §14.3 lines 2146-2168 (coordinate system — read before writing placement code)

## Done when
- All three modes produce output through `Quire.Compose` from PDFium layout spans: overlay preserves the original underneath, sidecar produces bilingual side-by-side pages, replace substitutes in place.
- A 20-page fixture translated in each mode preserves layout acceptably, with the translated text positioned per §14.3 (correct on rotated and cropped pages).
- Replace mode is labelled best-effort in the UI, consistent with §9.11 line 1789.
- The job runs in an Oban queue with progress reporting and emits telemetry; results are stored as a new revision via `Storage`.

title: T-161: Consent and provider disclosure in Settings, default off
description:
## Task
Consent and provider disclosure in Settings (§11.3): which provider, what leaves the machine, retention. Translation is the only v1 feature that sends **document content** to a third party — the setting defaults to off (`Provider.Null`) and the tab says so plainly.

## Spec
- plan3.md §11.3 lines 1950-1960 (Settings: Privacy & translation — provider, consent, data retention)
- plan3.md §9.11 lines 1799-1810 (`Provider.Null` is the default; translation is the only v1 feature that hands a third party the text of the user's document)

## Done when
- The Privacy & translation settings tab names the configured provider, states exactly what leaves the machine, and states the retention policy.
- The setting defaults to off (`Provider.Null`) on a fresh install, and no real provider can be invoked until consent is explicitly recorded.
- With `Provider.Null` configured the Translate tab renders and explains itself, and makes **no network call** — asserted by a test that fails on any outbound request.
- Revoking consent in Settings immediately returns the app to `Provider.Null` behaviour without a restart.
- The tab is keyboard accessible, has light and dark variants, and uses plain language rather than engine or provider output.

title: T-160: Cost estimation + translation_cache keyed by sha256(text)+langs
description:
## Task
Cost estimation + caching in `translation_cache` by `sha256(text)+langs`.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.11 lines 1795-1797 ("Text length is billable — show an estimated cost/token count before running, and cache by `sha256(text) + langs` in `translation_cache` (§5.5)")
- plan3.md §5.5 lines 793-818 (`translation_cache` schema)

## Done when
- An estimated cost/token count is shown before a translation job is started, and the user must confirm before any provider call is made.
- `translation_cache` rows are keyed by `sha256(text) + source lang + target lang`, per §5.5.
- Re-translating a document whose text is unchanged issues **zero** provider calls — asserted with a mock provider that fails the test if invoked a second time.
- Changing only the target language produces a cache miss and a fresh call, proving langs are part of the key.

title: T-159: Selection translate popup, translate comments, glossary
description:
## Task
Selection translate popup; translate comments; glossary.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.11 lines 1790-1792 (**Selection translate** | C→S | Translate the current text selection into a popup; **Glossary** | C | Per-document term overrides that the translator must honour; **Translate comments** | S | Translate annotation contents rather than page text)

## Done when
- Selecting text in the viewer offers a translate action that returns the translation in a popup without modifying the document.
- Translating comments rewrites annotation contents only and leaves page text untouched, asserted against a fixture with annotations.
- Per-document glossary terms are honoured: a term with an override is never returned untranslated or translated differently, verified by a test that supplies a glossary and asserts the output.
- The popup and glossary editor are keyboard accessible with `aria-label` on icon-only controls, have light and dark variants, and implement loading and error states.

title: T-158: Shrink-to-fit + overflow reflow handling with a review list
description:
## Task
Shrink-to-fit + overflow reflow handling with a review list.

## Spec
- plan3.md §9.11 lines 1812-1815 ("**Reflow is the hard part.** Translated text is routinely 20–40 % longer than the source. Implement: shrink-to-fit within the original bbox down to a minimum size, then overflow into a footnote block, and mark such regions in a review list.")

## Done when
- Translated text is shrunk to fit within the original bbox down to a defined minimum font size before any other strategy is applied.
- Text that still does not fit at the minimum size overflows into a footnote block rather than being clipped or silently dropped.
- **Every** region that was shrunk below the original size or overflowed is listed in the review list, and clicking an entry navigates to that region — verified on a 20-page fixture where the expected overflow count is known.
- A test with deliberately long translated strings asserts no text is lost in any of the three modes.

title: Gate 11: layout preserved, overflows flagged, Null makes no calls
description:
## Acceptance gate
**Gate 11:** translation of a 20-page document preserves layout acceptably and flags every overflowed region in the review list; with `Provider.Null` configured the tab renders, explains itself and makes no network call; the cache prevents a re-translation of unchanged text.

## Verify
1. Translate a 20-page fixture and confirm the output preserves layout acceptably in each of the three modes (overlay, sidecar, replace).
2. Confirm every region that overflowed or was shrunk below its original size appears in the review list, against a fixture whose expected overflow set is known — none missing.
3. With `Provider.Null` configured (the default), open the Translate tab: it renders, shows the "translation disabled" explanation, and issues no outbound network request.
4. Re-run a translation over unchanged text and confirm `translation_cache` serves it with zero provider calls.

value: macOS 27: mix-downloaded standalone binaries (tailwind, esbuild) are SIGKILLed (exit 137) by Gatekeeper. The plan's §3.6.6 fix 'xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine' does NOT work — the attribute is com.apple.provenance, which xattr cannot remove, and spctl reports an invalid ad-hoc signature. The working fix is 'codesign --force -s - <binary>'. xattr -cr alone can itself break an ad-hoc signature. See pdf-0k9a.
